answers.Personal background: Joe Miller, a native of Haddon Heights, New Jersey, has a strong background in political science and sociology, having graduated from Baptist Regional High School and the University of Maine in Orono. Joe’s dedication to public service is evident through his election to the school board in Audubon, New Jersey, in 2020. Furthermore, his commitment to education extends beyond his local community, as he has also represented Camden County on the New Jersey School Boards Association Board of Directors. Joe’s journey exemplifies his passion for community involvement and his dedication to making a positive impact on education in his region. Currently, Joe works as a Realtor with Keller Williams, combining his community-oriented spirit with his expertise in real estate. Additionally, he is an active member of his local Rotary chapter, further demonstrating his commitment to service and community engagement.
answers.Political background: Joe Miller’s political background is a testament to his unwavering commitment to civic engagement and public service. During his time at the University of Maine, where he earned a degree in political science with a minor in sociology, Joe was not only a dedicated student but also actively involved in shaping campus life. He served as a senator on the student government and has continued to pursue his passion for politics. Currently, he holds the position of chairman of the Camden County Young Republicans, a role that showcases his leadership and dedication to advancing conservative ideals within his community. Joe’s journey, from his student government days to his current leadership in the Young Republicans, highlights his enduring commitment to political engagement and his active role in shaping the future of his region.
answers.Why are you running for office?: Joe Miller has stepped up as a dedicated candidate for the New Jersey State Assembly in the 5th Legislative District, driven by a passionate desire to ensure that the voices of the voters are heard. He’s grown tired of unanswered questions, unfulfilled promises and rising taxes. Joe’s campaign is rooted in a commitment to transparency, accountability and fiscal responsibility. His aim is to represent the concerns and aspirations of his constituents, striving for a government that truly serves the people and addresses their needs. With a firm resolve to bring about positive change, Joe Miller’s candidacy symbolizes his determination to create a better future for the community he cares deeply about.
answers.Key election issue: Joe Miller’s campaign for the New Jersey State Assembly in the 5th Legislative District centers on the crucial issue of parental choice and involvement in their child’s education. Joe firmly believes that parents should have a direct and meaningful role in shaping their children’s educational journeys. He advocates for policies that empower parents to make informed decisions about their child’s schooling, whether it’s choosing the right school for their needs or having a voice in curriculum decisions. Joe’s commitment to parental choice and involvement underscores his dedication to strengthening the connection between families and education, ensuring that parents have the tools and opportunities to actively participate in their children’s educational development.
answers.Example of a successful project: During his tenure as a school board member in the Audubon Public School District, Joe Miller spearheaded a highly successful grade and score conversion project that significantly streamlined the process for students transferring into the district. This project was a game-changer, as it ensured that students’ grades from their previous schools seamlessly correlated with Audubon’s grading system. Joe’s leadership and dedication to this initiative not only simplified administrative procedures but also alleviated the stress that often accompanies transferring schools, enabling students to transition more smoothly into the district. His visionary approach exemplifies his commitment to enhancing the educational experience and creating a more inclusive and welcoming environment for all students in Audubon.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: Joe Miller faces the unique challenge of being a young candidate running for office, but he’s turning this challenge into an asset. While his age may raise questions for some, Joe leverages his fresh perspective, boundless energy and innovative ideas to connect with a new generation of voters. He demonstrates that youth can bring a valuable, forward-thinking approach to politics, unburdened by traditional paradigms. Joe’s ability to engage with diverse age groups, coupled with his commitment to his community and his impressive track record, showcases his determination and capacity to overcome age-related concerns. He inspires confidence by proving that age is no obstacle when passion, dedication and a vision for a better future drive his candidacy.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: Joe Miller is committed to crafting more equitable gun laws in New Jersey that strike a balance between responsible gun ownership and safety. He firmly believes that responsible gun owners should have access to the tools and knowledge necessary to ensure safe firearm usage. Joe advocates for robust firearm safety education programs, emphasizing responsible handling and storage. He also understands that overly restrictive laws can inadvertently make it easier for criminals to obtain firearms, as they often bypass legal channels. Joe’s approach focuses on sensible legislation that safeguards the rights of responsible gun owners while addressing the root causes of gun violence through education and comprehensive solutions, ultimately creating a safer environment for all New Jersey residents.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: Joe Miller is a strong advocate for environmentally friendly initiatives and the transition to “go green.” He recognizes the importance of sustainable practices in preserving our planet for future generations. However, Joe also understands the critical need for responsible research and assessment when it comes to certain projects, such as offshore wind. While renewable energy sources like offshore wind hold great potential for reducing carbon emissions, he believes that a thorough examination of their impact on wildlife is essential. Joe’s stance underscores the necessity of balancing environmental progress with a commitment to protecting our natural habitats and wildlife, ensuring that our pursuit of sustainability is both effective and responsible.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: Joe Miller is a staunch advocate for fiscal responsibility in New Jersey, firmly believing that the state must reduce spending to alleviate the burden of high property taxes on its residents. He understands that excessive government spending directly impacts property taxes, making homeownership less affordable for many. By implementing measures to decrease spending, Joe aims to create a ripple effect that not only benefits property owners but also lowers the overall cost of living in the state, including reduced rent for tenants. His commitment to fiscal prudence is not only a path to lower property taxes but also a means to enhance the overall economic well being of all New Jersey residents.

answers.Personal background: I was born in Philadelphia and raised in Willingboro. I am a graduate of Rowan University. I have worked in government, organized labor and private sector positions over the course of my professional career. Additionally, I am currently a member of the Carpenters Union Local #255.
answers.Political background: I was first elected to office in November 2011 to the New Jersey General Assembly and served there until my election to the state Senate in November 2017. I now serve as the Senate majority whip.
answers.Why are you running for office?: I am running for office to continue my advocacy on behalf of the residents of the 7th Legislative District. I pride myself on being an accessible and forceful advocate for the 17 communities that I am privileged to represent.
answers.Key election issue: Making New Jersey more affordable is an important component of my focus as an elected official. Whether that is the work I have led on lowering prescription drug costs or supporting historic property tax relief through the ANCHOR program, being laser-focused on making our state more affordable will always be my top priority.
answers.Example of a successful project: I proudly authored the nation’s first and only Environmental Justice Law. This law ensures that no community will have a greater environmental burden than benefit. It requires the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection to analyze the cumulative impacts of a project on a community before granting a new permit or a renewal for certain types of facilities that have the potential to be hazardous to the community in which they are located.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: The biggest challenge that I face is the difficulty in overcoming the inertia of the government process. There are big challenges that our state has historically faced, and the fierce urgency to address and remedy those challenges isn’t always handled with the speed I would like.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: I think New Jersey’s gun laws strike a reasonable balance between protecting our citizens without undermining our country’s Second Amendment rights. It is why our state has one of the lowest rates of gun deaths per capita in the nation. Most recently, I have authored a new law that increases penalties for illegal gun trafficking.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: Our state’s and frankly our nation’s goal of combating climate change is a quality of life, sustainability and security issue that we can no longer delay. The challenge is that the misinformation surrounding these goals, often for political expediency, tends to overshadow thoughtful debate around how we best combat climate change. I believe that in order for us to aggressively target this issue we need an “all of the above” energy aggregation goal that utilizes all sources of clean energy as we transition away from our sole dependency on traditional fossil fuels.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: The main challenge in this area is the lack of supply. Housing inventory is at a low point, and that forces pricing to go higher and shuts out so many from purchasing a home. I am proud of my work to augment New Jersey’s Affordable Housing Production Fund, which will create a significant number of housing units across our state. This, coupled with the work I have led to provide financial resources for first-generation homebuyers and down payment assistance, is geared toward expanding both inventory and access to the American dream of home ownership.

answers.Personal background: I am serving my third term representing the 7th Legislative District in the New Jersey General Assembly and am a member of the legislative leadership, holding the position of majority whip. I was elected in 2017 and am the first woman in over 20 years to represent the 7th Legislative District in the Assembly. Prior to serving in the Legislature, I worked at the New Jersey Schools Development Authority, serving as the community relations manager, where I established a transparent government records division and worked closely with communities to address local and environmental concerns. These efforts led to the building and modernizing of public schools, improving classrooms across New Jersey. As a chief of staff and policy director in the Legislature, I worked on major public policy initiatives that included pay equity, fair wages, women’s health care, gun violence, state debt reduction, prescription drug affordability, property tax relief and economic growth.
answers.Political background: I have been involved in politics since mid-1995. I worked on my first race as the scheduler and events coordinator; in 1997 I ran for the Marlton Township Council and then for the Assembly in 2001. In 2000 I served as the Burlington County treasurer. I volunteered and worked with DACC from 2002 through 2016. In 2017 I won an Assembly seat in the 7th Legislative District. In the 2023 election cycle I am running for my fourth term for the next two years.
answers.Why are you running for office?: All of my work life I have been learning and working in customer service, helping people, whether it was as a litigation paralegal, community manager for schools development, chair of the recreation advisory committee, staffer for legislators or now as a legislator. I wanted to be in a position that gives me the satisfaction of helping others and being needed. I realized that being a legislator is something I have been working toward all of my working life.
answers.Key election issue: Affordability for all New Jerseyans. Assuring that our residents can live, raise a family, work, get a strong education, play and retire in New Jersey. Affordable and accessible health care; physical, emotional and mental health is a top priority, especially for our youth. All issues are on the table and impact our families.
answers.Example of a successful project: I have had a few bills signed into law by the governor, including creating parking placards for our home health-care workers, Students Bill of Rights Food Insecurity and a Licensure Compact for our teachers, and I established an Ireland Trade Commission in the Department of State, to name just a few.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: Many of my challenges have occurred with reaching my short-term goals, including leadership, in which I am honored to serve as the majority whip. I worked hard to overcome the challenges I faced, with persistence and perseverance. Along with dedication and commitment to myself, the office and work as a public servant.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: I’m proud that we have taken important steps in the Legislature to combat the epidemic of gun violence by fighting for common-sense laws that protect our residents. For example, I supported reducing the size of high-capacity magazines that are often used in mass shootings, because they are a danger to public safety and have no place in our communities; strengthened background checks and required background checks for private gun sales, and prohibited the sale of deadly body-armor-piercing ammunition.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: We have a moral responsibility to address the alarming threat of climate change, and I’m working toward this by improving the availability and accessibility to electric vehicle charging infrastructure, reducing energy consumption and emissions, establishing new financing mechanisms to give property owners the ability to make energy-efficient improvements, and requiring local governments to consider the risks of climate change when making planning decisions. Furthermore, I’m working toward increasing capacity for renewable energy production, establishing a solar incentive program, creating large-scale solar facilities and positioning New Jersey to be a world leader in offshore wind energy production that will also create tens of thousands of new jobs. And ensuring that everyone has access to clean drinking water by making historic investments in water infrastructure projects and improving the safety of drinking water.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: Our local small businesses are the backbone of our economy and our communities. To support a thriving economy we must ensure businesses can succeed while supporting our workforce by providing incentives for job creation and capital investment, disbursing financial resources for small businesses, attracting film studios for large-scale production projects, and maximizing the benefits of Urban Enterprise Zones. Furthermore, we must improve our economy through comprehensive economic incentives to prioritize investments in high-growth sectors and creating viable job opportunities to position New Jersey as a global leader in the innovation economy. And, by supporting cultural, historic, food and beverage tourism, including online gaming and sports wagering, enabling fixed-odds horse wagering and investing in the promotion of local tourism and historical and agricultural industries, we can bolster economic opportunities in every region of our state.

answers.Personal background: I am a US History teacher at Hammonton High School and president of the Hammonton Education Association. I aim to bring a unique and much-needed perspective to the Legislature of what it takes to help our students and schools succeed. My parents were both casino gaming employees, and I worked my way through college by working in an Atlantic City casino. My wife, Tracy, is also a public school teacher, and we are proud parents of two children.
answers.Political background: As Hammonton Education Association president, I have worked on organizing union members for political action to elect candidates who are education advocates. With the NJEA, I have contributed to candidate screenings for the NJEA’s endorsements. Additionally, after Donald Trump was elected, I got involved with the Hammonton Democratic Club to focus on turning out voters locally. I became a local political leader and serve as the Democratic municipal chair of Hammonton, coordinating closely with the Atlantic County Democratic Committee and assisting the party chairman with countywide efforts.
answers.Why are you running for office?: Education comprises a significant portion of the state budget, yet very few teachers run for state office. I think more educators should be involved in government to improve education legislation. Education is foundational to American opportunity; a good education can help level the playing field and give our students their best chance to succeed. I will be a strong voice for our children and understand that in order for them to flourish now and in the future, they need to grow up in a thriving local economy where people aren’t just struggling to get by.
answers.Key election issue: Making New Jersey more affordable is critical. As we have been knocking on doors and talking to voters, affordability and property taxes are the concerns that voters bring up the most. It is clear that our state needs to make changes to make New Jersey affordable for families and for seniors to stay and retire here.
answers.Example of a successful project: My union, the Hammonton Education Association, partners with the Hammonton Green Committee and Hammonton Town Council to organize a communitywide cleanup where we recruit hundreds of students to help clean up the town every spring. This event teaches students the value of community service at a young age.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: Working as a teacher and serving as the Hammonton Education Association president through the COVID-19 pandemic presented obstacles in our schools that we had never seen before. Prioritizing the educational experience while protecting the health and safety of students, their families and educators required creative solutions. I focused on clear communication with union members and administrators to make sure all understood how changes were affecting students and educators so that improvements could be made quickly when needed.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: We must be at the forefront of legislative solutions that are focused on combating the influx of guns into our communities and limiting the concealed carry of handguns in New Jersey. We must continue to raise awareness about our red-flag laws and how to utilize them to issue gun violence protective orders against people who pose a significant threat to themselves or others by possessing a firearm. We must continue supporting common-sense gun legislation that protects our children, residents and communities. Gun violence in schools is a major concern, and all safety measures possible should be taken to protect our students and school staff members. Regarding the law that was challenged in federal court, it is key to have enforcement mechanisms for gun sellers who act recklessly and put communities at risk.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: Preparing our workforce for union jobs in the renewable energy sector will be critical. Green jobs are the fastest-growing segment of New Jersey’s economy, with 7,000 new jobs in offshore wind and 6,000 jobs in solar energy expected in southern New Jersey over the next 10 years. Creating the right incentives to continue the transition to renewable energy is very important and should be done with support to overcome the costs and obstacles for producers and consumers.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: The StayNJ senior property tax credit is an important step to relieve the tax burden, but many feel the strain of property taxes long before retirement. We must evaluate state spending and improve cost efficiency while maintaining quality services. Efforts to grow the economy can positively impact middle class families, so the Legislature should continue to promote developing industries. To support a thriving economy, we must ensure businesses can succeed while supporting our workforce. We can achieve this by providing incentives for job creation and capital investment, disbursing financial resources for small businesses, and investing in local tourism, historical, and agricultural industries.

answers.Personal background: I am a mother of three, a former Chesterfield Township School Board member and committeewoman, and the communications director at the Fair Funding Action Committee, a bipartisan grassroots group that advocates for increased school funding. I use my voice for children with special needs and increased behavioral and mental health services for children. My husband Jonathan and I live in Chesterfield Township.
answers.Political background: I served as a Chestefield Township committeewoman and worked to implement the Chesterfield Township Parks and Recreation Master Plan. I was a member of the Chesterfield Township Alliance Against Substance Abuse. I then served on the Chesterfield Board of Education and was able to elevate the concerns of parents and students, especially during the educational challenges of the pandemic. To correct the underfunding of my children’s school district, I became an education policy advocate and communications director of the Fair Funding Action Committee, a bipartisan grassroots group that advocates for increased school funding.
answers.Why are you running for office?: During my life, I’ve experienced hardships and understand how families need affordable health care, good public schools for their children, job opportunities and smart public policy to address our affordability crisis. As a mother of three turned public policy advocate, I know that meaningful change is possible. As a state lawmaker, I will be a problem-solver, bringing new ideas and fresh approaches to the state Capitol.
answers.Key election issue: Protecting reproductive freedoms in New Jersey is a top priority for me. We must continue to protect women’s access to reproductive health-care services, including abortion. Women’s reproductive health and the decision to have an abortion should be left to the women and their doctors, not the government.
answers.Example of a successful project: When I discovered that my children’s school district was lacking funding, I began to research NJ education funding and discovered that the allocation was not updated to reflect changes in enrollment, leading to years of underfunding in Chesterfield. I then organized a coalition of parents across the state to advocate for fair funding, and we were able to pass legislation that has increased funding for districts that have been underfunded for years.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: Two of my children have had mental health diagnoses, so I became an advocate for them as individuals and for broader mental health support and resources for our youth. My youngest, Molly, has become a mental health care advocate herself, and we have met with legislators to push for increased support for youth mental health. Supporting children with mental health needs requires a strong care network, and I want to make those systems easier to access and navigate for families.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: No one should have to live in fear of gun violence, and I support common-sense gun safety measures to keep us all safe. New Jersey now has some of the strongest gun laws in the nation, but we must do more on a community level. We need religious, civic, community and business leaders working together to foster responsible gun ownership and create a culture where gun violence is not tolerated. While the law challenged in federal court is now out of the Legislature’s hands, I support measures that hold those accountable who have contributed to gun violence. Gun safety is also a crucial piece of suicide prevention. My mother committed suicide with a gun after moving out of New Jersey to a state with looser regulations. There is a correlation between suicide rates and gun ownership rates by state, and it is essential that in New Jersey we pass legislation that also protects people who could be harmful to themselves.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: We have an excellent opportunity to be a national leader in renewable energy production in South Jersey. Investing in offshore wind, solar and hydrogen power will reduce our carbon footprint and have significant economic impacts on our region. Moving toward greater use of electricity can be a step toward sustainable energy, but I believe it should be accomplished with incentives and education for consumers and with understanding of supply chain shortages and costs rather than through mandates.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: New Jersey property taxes put a strain on many families, sometimes forcing them out of the state to pursue more affordable options. At the state level, we need to find ways to ease the burden of property taxes. Legislation like StayNJ, which provides tax credits to seniors under a certain income threshold, can be part of the solution. Our state is facing an affordability crisis; our residents, seniors, veterans and small business owners need smart public policies to address their challenges. We must lower the government’s cost while ensuring that residents get the highest quality of services they deserve and embrace policies to make our state more affordable.

answers.Personal background: I was raised in Lakewood by hardworking immigrant parents – a nurse’s aide mother and an entrepreneurial father – along with a stepfather who served as a police officer. After high school, I founded a computer recycling and repair company before transitioning into IT management at an investment firm. I then worked my way through Ocean County Community College as a carpenter, ultimately earning a bachelor’s degree from Seton Hall University. My desire to make a difference led me to serve as a humanitarian aid missionary during summers. Later, I attended Valparaiso University School of Law on a full Jurist Scholarship. My career has been diverse, spanning executive leadership, general counsel roles for nonprofits and finance. I am also a founding officer of Jeff’s Camp – A Home for Heroes, a veterans support organization, and serve in other registered not-for-profits. Actively involved in various community organizations and causes, I own a home in Little Egg Harbor and currently reside there with my wife, Dimple, and our dog, Russell. I am now eager to leverage my experience and community-focused vision in a bid for the New Jersey State Senate.
answers.Political background: I’ve always been a voter, but I’m relatively new to politics and only became actively involved in 2016 when I learned about Citizens United and the corrupting influence of money in politics – a scourge I’ve been fighting against ever since. I also realized how important primaries are and dove into partisan politics. I put my legal experience to work as part of Sen. Bernie Sanders’ nonpartisan voter protection team to make sure everyone who was entitled to vote was able to. I then took on more responsibilities, winning an election to become municipal chair of my township’s Democratic Party and also president of Great Bay Democrats, a 501(c)4 organization representing Little Egg Harbor, Tuckerton and Eagleswood. I’ve also extended my commitment to public service by joining the Little Egg Harbor Environmental Commission, focusing on sustainability issues in my community.
answers.Why are you running for office?: I’m running for office driven by a deep-seated desire to contribute to the greater good and tangibly improve the lives of the people in New Jersey. Growing up in poverty provided me with a unique lens through which to view the struggles of disadvantaged communities, and this perspective motivates me to confront these challenges head-on. My experience in nonprofit governance, business leadership, law and finance equip me with the knowledge and skills to effectively address the complex issues facing our communities. Having already put this commitment to service into action in numerous ways, I believe I’m uniquely positioned to represent and advocate for all New Jerseyans. I’m deeply committed to ensuring that our policies prioritize the needs of every individual, regardless of their background or circumstances. And I would rather lose an election than betray my values or cave to monied interests. That’s why I’m running.
answers.Key election issue: One of the key pillars of my campaign is making New Jersey more affordable – more affordable to live in, more affordable to raise a family in, more affordable to do business in, and more affordable to retire in.
answers.Example of a successful project: As the vice president of workforce development at Friends in Action, I spearheaded a nationally recognized workforce development Initiative that served as a gateway into unionized construction trades. We collaborated with leading construction firms and community organizations in the Atlantic City area to provide at-risk young adults from underserved communities with comprehensive, union-led training in specialized fields such as carpentry, plumbing, electrical work and HVAC. Graduates were guaranteed job placements at union sites, offering them not just employment but a path to stable, union-backed careers. The program covered all costs, including living stipends, necessary tools and safety equipment, effectively transforming lives and uplifting communities.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: Growing up in a poor household, I gained firsthand experience with the challenges of poverty, and I also learned the vital importance of resourcefulness and resilience. These early life lessons not only shaped my character but also instilled in me a profound commitment to public service. When I later found myself as an executive at a large real estate developer, faced with the challenge of increasing revenue, I was adamant about not cutting staff or benefits – values that trace back to my upbringing. By employing Lean Six Sigma methodologies, I was able to critically assess inefficiencies across my company and our parent company’s subsidiaries, subsequently identifying waste and arbitrage opportunities. This led me to innovative solutions, such as leasing unused roof space to telecoms and consolidating services, which ultimately reduced our operating costs by approximately 60% without affecting our employees’ livelihoods.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: I am both a gun owner and a staunch advocate for common-sense gun laws in New Jersey. I believe that responsible gun ownership can coexist with measures aimed at enhancing public safety. My commitment to these principles is underscored by my recognition as a Moms Demand Action Gun Sense Candidate and my proudly held “F” rating from the NRA. I support bills that have been introduced, including those mandating firearms safety courses, imposing restrictions on certain .50-caliber firearms, and increasing penalties for manufacturing ghost guns. This also includes recently enacted legislation that empowers the attorney general to pursue certain gun industry businesses. Like most Americans, as indicated by polling, I endorse a balanced approach that upholds Second Amendment rights while prioritizing the safety of our communities. My stance on these issues is rooted in a commitment to both the Constitution and the well-being of New Jersey residents.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: I largely support the Murphy administration’s initiatives to combat climate change, as they are important steps to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and transition toward a sustainable energy future. However, I have reservations about some initiatives, such as completely banning gasoline cars, as I believe that it ignores the root of the problem. Instead of solely focusing on transitioning to electric cars, which have their own environmental concerns related to batteries and production, I advocate for significantly improving public transportation and building pedestrian-centric townships based on strong town principles. This approach can reduce the need for car ownership altogether, making it a more comprehensive solution to both transportation and environmental challenges.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: Addressing the cost of rent, housing affordability and property taxes is a cornerstone of my campaign, and to tackle the issues, I propose a holistic approach that encompasses several key initiatives. These include: continuing and expanding property tax relief programs like the ANCHOR and StayNJ programs to provide immediate relief to homeowners and renters while working on comprehensive, long-term solutions; expanding the Senior Freeze program to help seniors on fixed incomes stay in their homes by freezing property taxes; increasing affordable housing initiatives through grants, incentives and low-interest loans for developers; offering homebuyer assistance programs to level the playing field for first-time buyers; promoting innovative zoning to transform underutilized commercial areas into housing following “Strong Towns” principles; empowering community land trusts and utilizing publicly owned land for affordable housing; legalizing accessory dwelling units on single-family lots, and strengthening tenant protection laws to ensure fairness and stability for renters, ultimately creating more equitable and sustainable housing in New Jersey.

answers.Personal background: Born in Jersey City, raised in Toms River, I lived in Hudson County for many years. I’ve worked in corporate sales, information technology and education. I earned my B.S. from St. Peter’s University.
answers.Political background: This race is my first run for elective office. I can tell you that my political philosophy is left of center, and I have always voted accordingly.
answers.Why are you running for office?: Legislative District 9 is so reliably Republican that the Ocean County Democratic Committee frequently does not field a candidate in many races. The feeling, I suppose, is, “Why Bother?” Understandable (a Democrat has not held this seat since 1976), but not acceptable. The values of the Democratic Party should never be unilaterally surrendered, and should be a part of any election or policy debate.
answers.Key election issue: The danger represented by the rise of far right extremists in what used to be the Republican Party.
answers.Example of a successful project: As a political novice, I don’t have a record to share with you. Aside from politics, the completed project I’m happiest about is earning my B.S. as an adult student.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: Growing up fatherless had a huge impact on me as a parent. My response was to try to be the best father I could be, always being present when needed.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: Maintaining New Jersey’s assault weapons ban is priority #1. Guns in the home are the number one killer of children in this country. I advocate safe storage laws and universal background checks, including private sales and gun shows. I fully support the concealed carry law that is currently being challenged in court.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: I am fully in support of any green, renewable energy program. I understand coastal residents being concerned about the possible impact on their home’s value. My concern is that their homes will be worth nothing if they wind up under water – which is where we are heading if we don’t take steps to combat climate change.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: We must incentivize developers to build more affordable housing, be it through tax breaks or grants of some sort. The ANCHOR and Senior Freeze programs must continue. The amount of tax credits offered to seniors under the StayNJ program should be indexed to any local tax increases.
answers.Final thoughts: Win or lose, it has been an honor to participate in the political process.

answers.Personal background: I was raised in Point Pleasant, New Jersey, where I graduated from high school in 1962. I received a bachelor of arts degree from Monmouth University and a juris doctorate from Seton Hall University. I am a former Ocean County prosecutor and currently senior partner of Citta, Holzapfel and Zabarsky, Attorneys at Law in Toms River, New Jersey.
answers.Political background: New Jersey General Assembly 1994-2012, deputy Republican leader 2002-2003, assistant majority whip 1998-1999; New Jersey Senate 2012-present.
answers.Why are you running for office?: I am a lifelong resident of Ocean County. I want to continue to give back to Ocean and Monmouth counties and the State of New Jersey by taking on Gov. Murphy and the Trenton Democrats.
answers.Key election issue: There are two key issues in this election, to continue the fight for parental rights and the cost of living in New Jersey.
answers.Example of a successful project: I am proud to have been the sponsor of the laws that increased penalties for those who committed serious crimes while on bail, as well as the No Early Release Act, which requires certain offenders to serve at least 85% of their sentence before being eligible for parole.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: Since being in the minority it has been very challenging having many of your proposals defeated and prevented. I will continue to stand up for the people of New Jersey.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: New Jersey has some of the strongest regulations on guns. I would not change the law but let it be determined by the courts. The recent changes by Gov. Murphy appear to be unconstitutional.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: Our delegation has warned that Gov. Murphy’s extreme energy policies that would ban affordable natural gas will drive up energy costs for utility payers and make the state more unaffordable for low- and middle-income families.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: By stopping wasteful spending in New Jersey brought on by the Democrats in Trenton. A prime example of this is the budget that was passed earlier this summer. The $54.3 billion budget that was rammed down our throats lacked both transparency and accountability to the taxpayers of this state. Democrats provided no explanation for the more than $1 billion of pork that was added to the budget at the last minute.

answers.Personal background: I currently reside in Toms River, New Jersey. I received a bachelor of arts degree in history from Providence College and a juris doctorate from Seton Hall University School of Law. I am an attorney at Dasti, Murphy, McGuckin, Ulaky & Connors Law Firm.
answers.Political background: Toms River Council 2003, Toms River council president 2004-2011, New Jersey General Assembly 2011-present.
answers.Why are you running for office?: I want to continue the fight to get New Jersey back on the right path for our residents to work, live and raise families.
answers.Key election issue: I feel there are two key issues in this election, to continue the fight for parental rights and New Jersey’s cost of living.
answers.Example of a successful project: I led the fight to require the State Board of Education to finally return to in-person public meetings in 2023 after they had refused to do so since the beginning of the COVID-19 pandemic.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: It is extremely frustrating being in the minority and having our ideas and proposals thwarted time after time.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: I believe law-abiding citizens should not be subject to arbitrary restrictions placed on their fundamental constitutional rights simply because the majority party refuses to address the conduct of actual criminals.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: Our delegation has warned that Gov. Murphy’s extreme energy policies that would ban affordable natural gas will drive up energy costs for utility payers and make the state more unaffordable for low- and middle-income families. Taxpayers simply cannot afford the estimated $1.4 trillion price tag associated with electrifying their homes and businesses by replacing their natural gas stoves, furnaces and hot water heaters
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: By stopping wasteful spending in New Jersey brought on by the Democrats in Trenton. A prime example of this is the budget that was passed earlier this summer. No one had an opportunity to review this budget in committee, but Democrats rushed it through to avoid having to explain more than $1 billion of pork that was added at the last minute. There was no transparency during this budget process and zero accountability from the Democrats to the taxpayers of New Jersey.

answers.Personal background: Emma Mammano has been a Brick Township resident for over 20 years. She lives in the Midstreams neighborhood with her husband, Ronald Mammano, and their three children. Her 12-year-old daughter, Lia, attends Veterans Memorial Middle School, and her 15-year-old son, Santino, and her 17-year-old daughter, Gianna, attend Brick Memorial High School. Mammano has a master’s degree in child psychology from Southern Illinois University and a master’s degree in professional counseling from Monmouth University. She has worked as a mental health counselor with numerous populations, including youth in residential treatment and with adults in an outpatient substance-abuse setting. Mammano also has worked in the field of substance-abuse prevention, where she developed and implemented a number of innovative programs for middle and high school youth in Brick Township.
answers.Political background: Emma Mammano first ran for public office in 2017, when she ran for State Senate. She ran again for State Senate in 2021. In 2022, she was elected vice chair of the Ocean County Democratic Party. She is vice chair of the Brick Democratic Municipal Committee. In 2017, she founded the Democratic Women of Ocean County organization, to recruit and support women candidates for office.
answers.Why are you running for office?: Legislative District 10 deserves a hard-working, compassionate, responsive representative in the State House.
answers.Key election issue: Protecting the Barnegat Bay, storm/flood mitigation and preparedness for the Jersey Shore.
answers.Example of a successful project: I developed an arts program for middle school students to prevent substance abuse and other mental health issues.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: I suffered from postpartum depression after my first child. I sought professional help and reached out to friends and family for support. Consequently, I am also very concerned about maternal mental health and would create/support statewide initiatives to support new mothers.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: I wouldn’t change anything. I think every state should use New Jersey as a model, and if we had federal gun laws like the ones we have here, we could greatly reduce gun deaths. But without a federal standard, guns move freely from state to state and we are fighting a losing battle.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: I support them all, especially offshore wind. The Republicans have once again completely ignored science to rile up their base and win votes. We need action now to combat global warming, and this ridiculous narrative about offshore wind killing whales is a distraction. What the whales really need is for us to stop the ocean temperatures from rising even more.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: Consolidation of municipalities to share services. Fight at the federal level for tax relief (rebates and credits) for residents of New Jersey, which contributes more than its fair share to the federal budget and receives too little in return.

answers.Age: 44 Hometown: Government relations O: Raised in Point Pleasant Beach, graduated from Point Pleasant Beach High School. Went to college at Texas Christian University in Fort Worth, Texas. I started my career working for Congressman Chris Smith in his Washington and on the Helsinki Commission, working for human rights. My first full-time job was as field director for Congressman Mike Ferguson. I subsequently ran federal government relations for the Associated Locksmiths of America, the Reno-Sparks Indian Colony and CARFAX. Thirteen years ago, I started my own federal lobbying firm focused on giving a voice to those organizations that could previously not afford to have one. My firm has been profiled on the front page of the Washington Post, on Fox News and various other media outlets as we strive to even the playing field and create more transparency and accountability in government.
answers.Political background: In 2017, I was elected to the Point Pleasant Beach Council, where I served for two years. In 2019, I ran for mayor, defeating the incumbent in a primary election by roughly 20% and going on to win the general election by almost 75%. I serve on the board of the New Jersey Conference of Mayors and am actively involved in the Ocean County Mayors Association and Barrier Island Mayors Group.
answers.Why are you running for office?: I’ve been disheartened watching the majority in Trenton become more and more emboldened with their power and subsequently pass more and more extreme legislation. The out-of-touch actions they’ve exhibited are not indicative of New Jersey residents. I’ve seen firsthand the detrimental effects of their pandering policies on the Jersey Shore, our economy and our families. I plan on being a loud voice against all of it.
answers.Key election issue: Parental rights, wasteful spending of taxpayer money, stopping the offshore wind debacle, supporting our police and Increasing safety in all our communities, the degradation of personal accountability.
answers.Example of a successful project: As mayor of Point Pleasant Beach I’ve successfully led efforts to revitalize our historic downtown by focusing on measures that restore old buildings, recreate new ones and incentivize owners to do the right thing. I’ve safeguarded our town from destructive pop-up parties, cleaned up our beaches and boardwalk and stood hand in hand with law enforcement against damaging policies from Trenton. As a result, we’ve won multiple awards for preservation and tourism, brought families back in droves and saved family businesses.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: Finding dollars to revitalize a town without spending taxpayer money is one of the biggest challenges out there. We crafted a plan in Point Pleasant Beach to fix up blighted properties, therefore increasing the tax base. We’ve cut needless spending, refocused it and consolidated positions, like bringing our engineer in house. We’ve been aggressive with federal and state grant acquisition and I believe this skill set will be put to good use as I seek to help all of the 10th District towns do the same.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: As society becomes less and less safe with soft-on-crime policies, it’s important to maintain access for the public to protect themselves. The guns are already out there and no measures will ever keep them from criminals’ hands in the United States. I will support all reasonable measures allowing New Jersey residents to protect themselves, their families and their homes.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: I’m not sure how it helps our planet to use countless natural resources and diesel power to build thousands of non-recyclable wind turbines that destroy tourism, wind up in landfills and kill vital marine life. To me, that isn’t helping the climate or New Jersey in the slightest. When solar power becomes more aesthetically pleasing, more easily integrated, efficient enough and affordable enough, rooftops across the state will inevitably adapt that technology more and more. There’s no reason to force all the environmentally detrimental effects of windmills that only have a 20-year lifespan with more solar usage growing every year. You need only 100×100 miles of solar to run the entire country and that could easily be achieved as more rooftops are utilized.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: By stopping the spending of hundreds of millions of their dollars on offshore wind and the subsequent increase of their utility rates once the boondoggle of a project gets going. It also didn’t help our taxpayers that a billion dollars meant to give them utility relief was redirected to a Danish oil and natural gas company who stands to make untold amounts of money. If I can help reverse that, I will. Especially considering more international companies are subsequently lining up for taxpayer dollar handouts. Decisions like these are killing our taxpayers for the sake of corporate buyouts and campaign donors.
