answers.Personal background: I grew up in Freehold and volunteered for several area first aid squads in high school and college. I went to college at Penn State, earning my B.A. Back in Monmouth, I started several small businesses and joined the IBEW 400 Union in Wall Township. I earned my master’s from Rutgers and also served as an adjunct professor. I am also the proud founder of the Vin Gopal Civic Association, a nonprofit that serves the Monmouth community. I have served on many local boards within Monmouth County and have been state senator since 2018.
answers.Political background: I am a registered Democrat, but I am proud to be the most bipartisan member in the Senate, and work across the aisle whenever I can to deliver results for Monmouth County families.
answers.Why are you running for office?: I was lucky enough to be born and raised here in Monmouth County, and even luckier to be able to start a career and build my life here. I was inspired to run for office so I could fight in Trenton to make sure that more families can stay and thrive in our communities, all of our children have access to a great education, and businesses will open and grow in our communities. I know Monmouth County families deserve a senator in Trenton who puts their interests first 100% of the time, not just when it’s politically convenient. I have held on to that belief since I first took the oath of office, and I will continue to stand by that for as long as I have the honor to serve as Monmouth County’s state senator. Currently, I serve as Senate Majority Conference Leader and chairman of the Education Committee.
answers.Key election issue: Keeping Monmouth County families safe, making Monmouth County a more affordable place to start a family and stay here into retirement, and protecting health-care freedom
answers.Example of a successful project: I led the fight to successfully secure over $40,000,000 in historic mental health funding for our schools and communities in the newest state budget to tackle the mental health crisis facing teens today.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: Throughout my time in the Senate, I have worked across the aisle whenever possible, regularly held my party accountable, and always put Monmouth County families before political parties. I co-sponsored the bill to restrict the governor’s emergency powers to 60 days, I demanded the governor end the COVID testing requirement for unvaccinated teachers and school employees, and I have stood up to the governor and my party as they have instituted new mandates on electric stoves and electric vehicles. I have taken on these tough fights because my job is to represent the priorities and interests of Monmouth County’s families, not my political party.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: As senator, I have always put the safety of our families and communities first and supported common-sense gun laws. I have supported numerous pieces of gun violence prevention legislation and have always worked to bring stakeholders and constituents from all sides of the issue to the table as legislation is drafted. I voted for extreme risk protection orders to get guns away from dangerous people and sponsored legislation to make it harder for those who abuse animals to purchase a firearm. I was also just awarded the 2023 Moms Demand Action Candidate Distinction.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: While I support efforts to make New Jersey a more sustainable state, homeowners should be notified of any efforts that might directly impact their property values and rates. The burden should not be left to the taxpayers, ratepayers and homeowners to pay for the development and implementation of these types of projects, which is why I voted against an offshore wind bailout earlier this year. While I am supportive of efforts to transition to clean energy, the state’s Energy Master Plan has laid out aggressive goals that could carry steep costs for homeowners, ratepayers and taxpayers. I believe the state can promote clean energy without burdening hardworking New Jersey residents, and I will not support any mandate that requires a transition from natural gas to electric appliances, but will support incentives.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: This is a number one issue we are hearing about from constituents, as families are being priced out of their homes due to high property taxes and seniors are not able to stay here during retirement. It is why I sponsored StayNJ, the largest property tax relief program in New Jersey history, which will return to seniors 50% of their property taxes (up to $6,500). I also supported measures such as the ANCHOR property tax relief program and Senior Freeze, both of which provide financial relief for families and seniors who are struggling to afford to live in New Jersey.

answers.Personal background: I am a first-generation American, born and raised in Jersey City, New Jersey. My parents immigrated to the United States from Ireland and Ukraine. I graduated cum laude from Northeastern University with a degree in journalism and political science. Throughout my career, I have held leadership roles, including serving as the chief operating officer for Omnicom Group, where I worked with global advertising and marketing agencies. I also held vice president roles at Johnson & Johnson, working with senior leaders and global responsibilities and have experience in the public sector, including working with the Partnership for a Drug-Free America and managing communication for Phoenix House. My background and experiences have shaped my passion for making a positive impact and working toward social change.
answers.Political background: As a first-generation American, my passion for public service runs deep. Growing up in a household where hard work and determination were values instilled in me by my immigrant parents, I have always felt a strong sense of responsibility to give back to my community. While I may be a first-time candidate, my diverse background and 35+ years of experience in business and the nonprofit world have prepared me well for a role in public office. My unique perspective as the son of immigrants and my commitment to serving the people of Monmouth County will enable me to bring fresh ideas and a genuine desire for positive change to the table.
answers.Why are you running for office?: The current one-party rule in Trenton has neglected our state’s needs and resulted in numerous challenges for our county. The career politicians in charge have failed us, and their decisions do not benefit the people. We need fresh faces and new perspectives to bring about meaningful change in our state government. We cannot afford to wait any longer for things to improve. The current system is not working, and our community deserves better. That is why I am committed to fighting for the best interests of Monmouth County and bringing about the change we desperately need.
answers.Key election issue: Public safety and crime prevention have become critical concerns in my campaign here in Monmouth County. Our county has been known for its safe and supportive environment for families and professionals for years. However, recent events have shaken this reputation, such as the rise in home invasions in Fair Haven and Freehold and the robberies targeting small businesses in Long Branch and Eatontown. We must address these criminal activities directly and restore peace of mind to our citizens.
answers.Example of a successful project: Coming from a family of immigrants, I have always remembered my roots and the values of hard work and the pursuit of the American dream. Inspired by my parents’ journey, I have climbed the ladder of success, built a family and established myself in both the business world and the nonprofit sector. My decision to enter public office was driven by a genuine desire to serve. With a deep respect for individuals from all backgrounds, I am confident in my ability to collaborate with anyone in the Legislature, regardless of party affiliation.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: Throughout my career in business, I have frequently encountered unfamiliar business environments. However, I have discovered that effective leadership skills can be universally applied, regardless of the industry or organization. The key lies in actively listening to understand the specific problems and challenges and having the courage to ask fundamental and daring questions that lead to a comprehensive solution. By addressing the root cause of the issue, a roadmap can be created to empower everyone involved in overcoming the challenges and achieving success. I intend to bring this same leadership style and my problem-solving abilities as the next senator from the 11th Legislative District. Trenton needs to put its focus on producing results for the people of New Jersey.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: New Jersey has taken important steps toward eliminating illegal guns in our communities, but there is still work to be done to protect our residents. To address this problem, Assemblywoman Piperno, Assemblywoman Eulner and I believe in strengthening the punishments for those illegally possessing a firearm and using it in a crime and supporting community-based policing strategies to stop the flow of illegal weapons into our streets.
answers.On Murphy administration’s climate chang: While I support exploring all forms of green energy, as long as we do so honestly, responsibly and transparently, I believe it’s essential to implement a complete pause with all offshore wind development to understand the cause of the alarming mortality rate of marine life. Over 70 dead whales and 50 dead dolphins since December 2022, coinciding with an increasing number of sonar mapping boats, is concerning. My opponent calls people “conspiracy theorists” if they are concerned about a possible connection between sonar mapping and dead mammals. Instead of displaying arrogance and disrespect for these good people, we have listened to their concerns and advocated for a full-stop moratorium on offshore wind development and directing funds toward independent investigations to protect our ocean’s health. We must prioritize further research to determine the cause and take necessary precautions.
answers.How would you address the cost of rent,: New Jersey faces an affordability crisis, leaving seniors questioning whether they can afford to retire here. Senator Gopal and his Democratic colleagues have announced StayNJ as a solution – which would not take effect until 2026 (if ever) – but it fails to address the damage to seniors’ savings and quality of life. It is merely a superficial gimmick and temporary fix – a Band-Aid for an open wound. New Jersey residents need long-lasting tax cuts and real property tax relief to ensure they can keep more of their hard-earned money and retire comfortably.

answers.Personal background: I was born and raised in Essex County, but I learned to walk on the Long Branch boardwalk and have a lifetime of memories in Monmouth County, where I currently reside. I am a graduate of Duquesne University and Seton Hall School of Law. I am a practicing attorney and the managing partner of Peterpaul Law in Asbury Park. I was a longtime member of Garden State Equality and was the chair of the Garden State Equality Action Fund. I’ve served as a county prosecutor and, until this year, was a municipal court judge for the cities of Long Branch and Asbury Park.
answers.Political background: I am a Democrat, but I have a long record of bipartisanship. I was appointed as a municipal court judge in Long Branch by Republicans and Democrats on the city council. During my time at Garden State Equality, I helped pass New Jersey’s Anti-Bullying Bill of Rights by working with legislators from both sides of the political aisle. The legislation received bipartisan support, just one no vote, and it was signed into law by a Republican governor.
answers.Why are you running for office?: I was not eager to jump into electoral politics, but with my lifetime of law and advocacy experience, I believe I am the right candidate with the right experience to help solve the problems our state is facing. I know firsthand the toll that rising crime takes on families and communities, and I know what needs to be done at the state level to curb violence. I have partnered with law enforcement to take on criminals to keep families safe, and I will take this experience to the Assembly to protect Monmouth County families. I am also alarmed by the recent rollbacks in basic freedoms we have seen across the country. I have been and will always be a leader on protecting the rights and freedoms of women, those who are marginalized and vulnerable, and the LGBTQ+ community. In the Assembly, I will also work to lower the cost of living, invest in child care and elder care, and make it easier for families to live, work and stay in New Jersey through retirement.
answers.Key election issue: Keeping Monmouth County families safe, making Monmouth County a more affordable place to start a family and stay here into retirement, securing funding for mental health resources, and protecting health-care freedom.
answers.Example of a successful project: As a municipal court judge, I helped implement the Recovery Diversion Program, which provides second chances to those in the criminal justice system with substance abuse issues. The program has proven so successful that it is now a blueprint for similar programs across Monmouth County. I also co-authored New Jersey’s Anti-Bullying Bill of Rights with support from Republicans and Democrats in the legislature.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: I was part of the team that helped write and pass New Jersey’s Anti-Bullying Bill of Rights in the aftermath of the death of Tyler Clementi. I worked with Republican and Democrat lawmakers throughout all stages of the process. We shared a goal – protecting our kids – and with that goal we found a lot of common ground. When the legislation came up for a vote, it had widespread support from both parties and passed with just one no vote. It was signed into law by a Republican governor. I was able to accomplish the success of the Anti-Bullying Bill of Rights by listening and understanding the concerns about the impact of bullying. That is what I will do when elected.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: I was recently awarded the 2023 Moms Demand Action Candidate Distinction. In the Assembly, I will work to pass common-sense firearms legislation that is designed to keep our families and neighborhoods safe. I will work with Republicans and Democrats to make sure we are passing legislation that has widespread support and takes into account the voices of everyone in Monmouth County. I support recent moves in the Legislature to implement extreme risk protection orders to keep guns away from dangerous individuals and support Senator Gopal’s legislation that makes it more difficult for animal abusers to purchase firearms.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: Energy efficiency is important as we look to make New Jersey a more sustainable state. I support offering incentives when homeowners are making upgrades to existing structures or appliances, or when homebuyers are looking to build a new house from the ground up. The state can and should offer incentives to encourage energy-efficient construction, but I do not believe anyone should be forced to via mandate. We need to move towards more sustainable energy, but it should not only be up to individual taxpayers, ratepayers and homeowners to foot the bill.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: I support financing that would help create more housing in our state, especially when it comes to affordable housing. Too many families are being priced out of the housing market due to rising property taxes from the post-COVID housing boom. There needs to be a real partnership between the state and local municipalities to ensure that new housing construction is being optimized to provide more options for homebuyers. We must also look for more solutions to property tax rates and bills, just as the Legislature has recently done with property tax relief programs like StayNJ and ANCHOR. These programs will help seniors and families by returning large portions of their property tax bill to them so they have the ability to live, work and stay in New Jersey.

answers.Personal background: I am a lifelong Shrewsbury Borough resident, a devoted mother of two amazing sons and a proud Red Bank Regional High School graduate. With a degree in sociology from Washington College, I have worked in finance, specifically focused on commission management on Wall Street. Currently, I manage analytics for the financial and insurance industries at a data company in Eatontown. Additionally, I am a licensed real estate agent. My diverse experiences have shaped me into a well-rounded and resourceful individual passionate about helping others.
answers.Political background: Before my first term in the General Assembly, from 2018 to 2022, I had the privilege of serving as a Shrewsbury councilwoman, where I focused on ensuring the financial stability of the borough while preserving the services that our residents value. In 2020, I served as council president; in 2021, I was chairwoman of the open space committee. Throughout my tenure, one of my proudest accomplishments was successfully reducing the borough’s tax rate for multiple consecutive years, allowing our community to thrive and prosper without burdening our residents with excessive taxes. It was an honor to serve the people of Shrewsbury and work toward building a better future for our borough.
answers.Why are you running for office?: Our district is currently facing a critical problem as our representatives in Trenton need to be more effectively addressing the genuine concerns of the average person. As residents, we have high expectations that our representatives will prioritize and tackle the urgent issues that affect us daily. Ultimately, our goal is to serve the people of our district with honesty, openness and earnestness. By working together and prioritizing the interests of our constituents, we can overcome the challenges of partisan politics and positively impact the lives of those we represent. This unwavering dedication to public service will continue to guide us to create a better future for our district and the State of New Jersey.
answers.Key election issue: The rising mental health challenges among students are a cause for concern. We must recognize the increasingly complex issues our children face today, and our schools must provide comprehensive and accessible mental health support for our students. That’s why we are taking proactive measures to address these issues and remain deeply committed to securing sustained funding for our schools to implement safety measures, services and staff support that prioritize the mental well being of our students. Additionally, to address students’ mental health challenges, we acknowledge the importance of involving parents and honoring their fundamental right to be informed and engaged in their child’s mental health support and decision-making. We aim to empower parents by providing them the necessary tools and resources to create a comprehensive and inclusive mental health support system for our students.
answers.Example of a successful project: This year, despite the potential funding cuts to school-based mental health programs, Marilyn and I petitioned Gov. Murphy to reconsider his plan of delivering mental health support from regional hubs instead of immediate care at schools, a plan endorsed by Senator Gopal. We fought to save effective programs, like Red Bank Regional’s’ The Source, by engaging in conversations with the governor’s office and launching editorial and letter-writing campaigns. Thanks to our efforts and community support, we successfully preserved these school-based programs that benefit thousands of students.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: After my husband passed away, my family and I faced various financial and emotional hurdles. Suddenly, I dealt with the financial and emotional burdens of making ends meet, prioritizing bills and ensuring my children’s basic needs were met. I had to navigate the difficult choices of whether to put food on the table or gas in the car. Additionally, I worried about my children’s mental and physical well being during this stressful time. However, this situation has made me incredibly compassionate and understanding. It has motivated me to fight for those facing similar circumstances as a member of the Human Services Committee. I am proud of being able to make informed decisions on issues, such as affordable child care, financial hardship and the numerous difficulties that come with illness. Throughout this journey, I have learned to be resilient and resourceful, ultimately overcoming these challenges while being a devoted mother to my wonderful children.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: Fairer gun laws and comprehensive gun safety education are essential to ensuring the safety and well being of our entire community. By imposing stricter penalties that effectively discourage repeat violent offenders and restrict firearms access to individuals with a history of domestic violence, we can simultaneously protect our law-abiding and responsible gun owners and LD11 residents.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: We should promote innovation and advance cost-effective, dependable and clean technologies rather than mindlessly pursuing lofty and unattainable energy solutions in the name of pseudo-environmentalism. However, Gov. Murphy’s Master Energy Plan, which includes a proposal to shift to all-electric vehicles by 2035, will significantly restrict consumer options and render new cars unaffordable for the working and middle classes. Consequently, this will harm the automotive industry, its employees and the economy.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: We have introduced two bills to hold municipalities accountable for flouting employee vacation and sick pay laws, resulting in hundreds of millions of taxpayer dollars being misused. Our proposed bills would establish additional oversight measures, such as requiring municipalities to publish their payment policies on their websites or the Department of Community Affairs’ site and creating an Office of Leave Time Compliance to ensure compliance with sick and vacation leave policies. Closing the loopholes and enforcing the existing reforms is crucial to providing substantial property tax relief.

answers.Personal background: I grew up in Maryland, but my education and career in medicine brought me to the tri-state area, and, eventually, Monmouth County. I attended Middlebury College before receiving my master’s in health policy from Yale and my medical degree from the University of Rochester. I am a board-certified doctor of rehabilitation and physical medicine and now work with patients in Monmouth County, focusing on senior care, in honor of my Grandma Millie. I am the deputy mayor of Ocean Township and have been on the council since 2019. I am a mom to two daughters, Amalia and Vera, and if elected, I will be the first female practicing physician ever elected to the Legislature.
answers.Political background: As deputy mayor, I ran twice on a bipartisan ticket. I work daily with Republicans and Democrats on a nonpartisan council to get results for Ocean Township. While I am a Democrat, I feel that the best outcomes result in hearing from both sides of the aisle and working together, which is what I do every day.
answers.Why are you running for office?: I was first inspired to run for office in 2016, when I saw there was a need for more women in leadership positions. It seemed more and more like we were being left out of the conversations, even with regards to our own bodies. As deputy mayor of Ocean Township, a board-certified rehabilitation doctor and avid surfer, I have spent my time in Monmouth County appreciating nature, fighting for Ocean Township residents, and improving patients’ lives through rehabilitation medicine. I decided to run for Assembly because I want to take those lessons and experiences and fight for those same goals and ideals in the Assembly. As someone who has taken the Hippocratic oath to do no harm, I am running so that I can make sure no one is harmed by decisions purely based on politics or made without proper consideration for those in Monmouth County. I will fight for fairer taxes so that working families of Monmouth County can afford to live here and seniors can afford to stay here. I will take my experience as a working mom raising my daughters to push for more services for our kids and families. I will fight to protect our environment and make sure it’s preserved for future generations.
answers.Key election issue: Keeping Monmouth County families safe, making Monmouth County a more affordable place to raise a family and stay here into retirement, and protecting health-care freedom.
answers.Example of a successful project: As deputy mayor of Ocean Township, I have consistently been a leader on environmental issues facing the town. As a member of the town Shade Tree Commission, I have helped pass new ordinances to preserve trees, reduce flooding and protect the environment. As a member of the Environmental Commission I have contributed to the development of ordinances addressing and reducing stormwater runoff. I also initiated the revitalization of the town’s “Green Team.” Annually, this team is responsible for the “Green Fest,” a festival to bring environmental ideas and vendors to Ocean Township to help educate across generations. Lastly, I am a member of the Deal Watershed Alliance, where I am working on projects to reduce silt water filling in the lake to improve water quality. This has had a direct impact in increasing recreational access to the lake.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: I work every day on behalf of my patients to give them the care and treatment they deserve. That often means fighting with insurance companies on my patients’ behalf to advocate for their needs. I have seen up close the reality of what happens when patient care is sacrificed because of bad health-care policy, and it can be challenging to fight against these policies and large corporations. I went into medicine to help people, and I am running for the Assembly for the exact same reason. In the Assembly, I will take my experience in medicine and health-care policy and work to put the needs of patients at the forefront of our health-care system, just as I do every day as a doctor.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: I was just awarded the 2023 Moms Demand Action Candidate Distinction. In the Assembly, I will support common-sense gun laws that keep our families and communities safe. I will bring together constituents from all sides of the issue to make sure they have a voice in legislation being drafted. I support recent measures taken by the Legislature to implement extreme risk protection orders to get guns away from dangerous people and support Senator Gopal’s bill that makes it more difficult for animal abusers to purchase guns.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: I agree that we need to be working as a state to make it more sustainable. However, it should not be left to the taxpayer to pay for these changes. We need to make sure that the efforts to transition to clean energy are not costing homeowners, ratepayers or taxpayers, and that we promote clean energy in non-detrimental ways for families. I would not force mandates on New Jersey residents. State incentives are the best route for achieving efficiency goals.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: As deputy mayor of Ocean Township, the biggest issue I hear about from constituents is property taxes. Older families are getting priced out of the homes they have raised their kids in. Young families are trying to buy their first home and simply cannot afford it. I strongly support the historic tax relief programs, StayNJ and ANCHOR, that will help seniors and families to afford to live and stay here. In the Assembly, I will focus on finding more legislative solutions that make New Jersey more affordable for everyone. I will work with local municipalities to make sure we are addressing property tax issues from the Statehouse down to the municipal level. There needs to be partnership at the state and local levels to ensure future housing investments are being done in a responsible and non-exclusionary manner, so that more residents are able to participate in the housing market. I also would support prioritizing upgrades and repairs to existing units, so we are not abandoning old housing that can be utilized.

answers.Personal background: I’m a Long Island native with a background in publishing and a passion for fitness and nutrition. After earning my bachelor’s degrees in literature and communications, I spent 20 years working on academic textbooks and consumer publications in the publishing industry. Along the way, I discovered a love for fitness and nutrition and pursued certifications in these fields. As a fitness instructor and nutrition coach, I strive to help individuals achieve their health and wellness goals by providing personalized workout plans and tailored nutrition guidance. I live in Colts Neck with my husband, Paul, and three wonderful children.
answers.Political background: After a successful publishing career spanning 20 years, I decided to prioritize raising my two sons and my daughter while actively engaging in community organizations. I volunteered with the Colts Neck Parent Teacher Organization and the education program at St. Mary’s Parish in Colts Neck. Additionally, I assumed the role of a youth sports coach, contributing my time and skills to the local community. In March 2017, I created an annual food drive benefiting three organizations: Lunch Break, the Center and Ronald McDonald House. This experience ignited my passion for advocating, volunteering and improving our community and it hasn’t stopped. As a working mom, handling today’s real world concerns makes us very much the truest representation of our voters. We were elected because we bring a fresh and untainted perspective to policy. We are grassroots, community-oriented and driven by common sense. By focusing on kitchen table issues, we will continue to bring that same dedication and passion to Trenton.
answers.Why are you running for office?: As working moms, Kim and I believe it is crucial to have more representatives like ourselves who can provide common-sense leadership in our district. However, the current voting record of Senator Gopal and the Democratic majority has hurt our community, negatively affecting our quality of life, safety and affordability. Two years ago, we ran for office to prioritize education, positive parent-teacher relations, community law and order, and affordability for our residents. We are earnest, energetic, and dedicated public servants and remain inspired to continue working for the well being and prosperity of the 19 municipalities we represent.
answers.Key election issue: First and foremost, a top priority is to restore the $70 million in state aid cut from LD11 school districts due to the passage of S2. Unfortunately, the current approach to school funding has devastated our students’ success. Despite the dire need for resources and improvements in our schools, Senator Gopal and the Democratic majority, who hold key positions, such as the chair of the Education Committee, have failed to address this issue adequately. Our students and educators are deprived of the quality education they deserve, putting their future at risk. We are committed to rectifying this situation and further advocating for the rights of parents and students in our district.
answers.Example of a successful project: In response to the appalling conditions faced by veterans residing in state-run nursing homes during the pandemic, we wasted no time taking action. Setting aside party differences, we collaborated with Democratic Assemblywoman Cleopatra Tucker on a crucial bill. This legislation aims to convert specific wards in the Menlo Park and Paramus veterans homes into single-occupancy rooms equipped with enhanced ventilation systems. To further address this issue, we proposed the establishment of a special committee tasked with investigating and preventing similar incidents from occurring in the future. Additionally, we are seeking bipartisan support for improved transportation access for our veterans. If we fail to come together for the well being of those who served our country, we should all be ashamed.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: A few months after our wedding, my father and my husband’s father faced serious health issues. We spent nearly every weekend driving between hospitals, juggling work and caregiving responsibilities. It was emotionally and physically exhausting, and we constantly feared losing our loved ones. Despite the overwhelming circumstances, we stayed positive and relied on prayer and support from family and friends. We made the most of our time with our fathers, even though it meant sacrificing our time and dealing with the strain on our careers. Sadly, we lost my dad and then my father-in-law within a few months of each other. It was a challenging time but it also brought us closer as a couple. We learned to lean on each other for support and to cherish the moments we had with our loved ones. Throughout it all, we remained united and have been married for 26 years. Our experience has given us a deep empathy for others, which is why Kim and I have so much compassion and prioritize health care, child care and senior care in New Jersey.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: We need to make the punishments for the illegal possession of firearms tougher. We must also focus on community policing to stop illegal guns from getting in. In addition, we must educate our local communities on law enforcement’s important role in keeping our neighborhoods safe. Engaging with community leaders and organizations will build a stronger sense of trust and understanding between the police and the community.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: I support efforts to protect the environment. However, we need a more balanced and practical approach to combating climate change than the governor’s proposed costly mandates to replace natural gas heating systems with electric heat pumps. Such mandates would be incredibly expensive for homeowners and financially strain businesses. Moreover, low-income households would be disproportionately affected, exacerbating their financial hardships. We must prioritize the financial stability of our taxpayers, businesses and infrastructure.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: The Fully Funding Schools and Cutting Property Taxes Act addresses high property taxes and underfunded public education in New Jersey. Sponsored by us, our plan would restore all S2 funding cuts, increase state aid to adequacy for all districts, and ultimately lower property taxes by an average of $804 in the first year, with ongoing reductions each subsequent year. By fully funding schools, we can successfully reduce property taxes while improving the education system in our state.

answers.Personal background: As a student growing up in Old Bridge, Mayor Owen Henry attended Voorhees Elementary School, St. Thomas the Apostle School and in 1977 he graduated from Cedar Ridge High School, now known as Old Bridge High School. Mayor Henry went on to earn a bachelor’s degree from Trenton State College (The College of New Jersey) in 1981.
answers.Political background: Mayor Henry has volunteered in several official roles. He served as an elected member of the Old Bridge Township Board of Education. He was appointed to the Old Bridge Planning Board and was an active member on the Old Bridge Environmental Commission.
answers.Why are you running for office?: To use my extensive experience in both the private and public sectors to fix the broken government in Trenton.
answers.Key election issue: Parental rights in their children’s education. Oppose radical and inappropriate school curriculums.
answers.Example of a successful projecy: Steering the financial status of Old Bridge Township in the right direction.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: When I came into office as mayor of Old Bridge Township, the financial status of the town was in jeopardy. It was a challenging time in our government, but with very tough choices made, the township’s financial status turned around. I am proud to say that the financial status of Old Bridge is stable and the township is thriving.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: I am a Second Amendment supporter. Laws addressing gun safety, use and necessity must be balanced, demonstrate efficacy and prevent unnecessary harm.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: Oppose reckless budgets and out of control spending

answers.Personal background: I have lived most of my life in Central New Jersey (Monmouth, Ocean and Mercer counties). I am a graduate of Trenton State College, where I earned a bachelor of science degree in law and justice. I also hold the designation of certified public manager through the State of New Jersey and Fairleigh Dickinson University. I recently retired at the rank of captain after 26 years in law enforcement with the New Jersey Division of Parole. I am an active union member and current vice president of the New Jersey Law Enforcement Commanding Officers Association. I am married and have two children, who attend the Jackson Township public school system.
answers.Political background: Previous to my current campaign for State Senate, I ran for town council in Jackson Township. I am also a second-term Ocean County Democratic County Committee member.
answers.Why are you running for office?: I know I can make a positive impact in the lives of people who live in my legislative district as well as the state. I want to make sure that all of the people that I will represent are treated fairly, with dignity and have the opportunity to be heard. Ultimately, I’m running for office because I want to help improve the quality of life for the people of New Jersey.
answers.Key election issue: There are several major issues that I feel are not being adequately addressed in New Jersey. One of the most pressing issues that needs immediate attention is mental health with respect to access, services and coordination. This is especially critical when considering the mental health needs of New Jersey’s children. So many preventable, negative outcomes tie into the lack of appropriate mental health services. If we can address a person’s mental health issues, we have a chance to help prevent problems, like drug and alcohol abuse, sexual abuse, adverse involvement in the criminal justice system and suicide.
answers.Example of a successful project: During my career with the New Jersey Division of Parole, I had the opportunity to be the lead or involved in several successful programs. Some of the most memorable programs include those that took a collaborative approach to solving a problem or providing needed services. One example is the Swift, Certain and Fair (SCF) program, which is a unique approach to working with opioid-involved individuals under parole supervision. It relies on various stakeholders to work together to help people stay drug free or initiate a quick and definitive response when relapse occurs. The ultimate goal is to get people the help they need, remain out of custody and receive appropriate treatment services. Incarceration would be the response only when all other avenues have failed. While the SCF approach was modeled after the HOPE probation program in Hawaii, it needed to be shaped to fit the parole supervision standards of New Jersey. As the commander of the district for the SCF pilot location, I was responsible for shaping, implementing and managing all law enforcement aspects of the program. The assessment of the pilot program reflected a reduction in recidivism for the group of parolees participating in SCF and earned the New Jersey State Parole Board the New Jersey Attorney General’s Initiative Award.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: I’ll give an example from when I was young and one of the first times I feel I was challenged. I broke my leg and had a cast on it for months. First, a full leg cast for about three months and then a lower leg cast for about another month or so after that. When I finally got out of the cast, I needed a cane, I walked with a bit of a limp, and I had gained a good amount of weight from being immobile. I was not happy with my condition and worried if I would be able to overcome these things. I decided that If I wanted to overcome them, I needed to take the steps that would get me to where I wanted to be. Although at times it was painful, through a regimen of long walks then running and working out, I was able to lose weight and fully regain my stride. This may seem like a minor challenge to some but I think for me it set my mind at a young age as to how I would face problems in the future and I learned that I was capable of overcoming adversities.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: New Jersey has very strong gun laws. Whatever changes I would advocate for or propose would be based on a common-sense approach on the issue. Ultimately, my goal, and what all elected official’s goal for this issue should be, is to ensure our citizens are safe from gun violence and that people who make our citizenry less safe because of the misuse of guns are held accountable. It’s the opinion of a federal court that recent legislation limiting the carrying of a firearm in certain locations is unconstitutional. I believe that the intent of this legislation was to protect people. If this legislation could be tailored to address the safety concerns while not being deemed unconstitutional, it should be reconsidered.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: I support efforts to combat climate change in general. I believe that we should look at all energy alternatives in an effort to fight climate change as there is a clear link between the burning of fossil fuels and the changing climate. I believe the best approach regarding things like electric cars and electric appliances is to make them more attractive to the consumer rather than outlawing gasoline-powered cars or gas stoves. I would propose we incentivize rather than ban.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: New Jersey certainly has its issues with the cost of rent, housing affordability and property taxes. One thing New Jersey is doing right is implementing tax relief programs, like the ANCHOR program and the new Senior Freeze program, both of which are Democratic-led initiatives. To reduce property taxes I would be on board with the initiative to return money to municipalities from the Energy Tax Receipts Property Tax Relief Fund that is currently going to the state. These millions of dollars should be returned and used in all municipalities with the specific purpose of reducing property taxes. With respect to the cost of rent, I would look at creating a new rebate program for families who are renters and are considered lower income earners. As for housing affordability, I would advocate for incentives to developers to create more affordable housing and to redevelop areas that can be revitalized.

answers.Personal background: Lifelong resident of Jackson, New Jersey. Graduate of the College of New Jersey. CEO of AdvicePay.
answers.Political background: Republican. Jackson Township Council; council vice president and president 2020. Assemblyman since 2022
answers.Why are you running for office?: To serve the residents of LD12
answers.Key election issue: Lowering property tax; lowering taxes overall; providing better services for veterans.
answers.Example of a successful project: Numerous press releases regarding work completed.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: Being in the minority in the Assembly, I’ve worked to find “common sense” legislation across the aisle and get bills passed into law. In less than 12 months I’ve had two bills passed to law.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: I voted against it and will continue to.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: No. I’m not against alternative sources of energy but it needs to be done right and economically.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: I would love them. I would take from the overinflated budget from things like $12 million to a French art museum in Jersey City to offset costs in other areas, including housing. I would also appoint a head of community affairs who actually does something, including lowering housing and energy costs.

answers.Personal background: I’m Raya Arbiol, and I’m proud to call Old Bridge, New Jersey, my hometown. I’ve been a resident of this community for most of my adult life. My educational journey has been driven by a thirst for knowledge, leading me to earn a master’s in business administration specializing in operations management from the University of Scranton, a master of science in information systems from Drexel University and an executive MBA from Rutgers University. Throughout my career, I’ve had the privilege of working in diverse industries, including health care administration, e-commerce, global supply chain and financial services. This professional diversity has given me a unique perspective on the challenges that our community faces. Beyond my career, I’ve always been deeply committed to service and have volunteered with various organizations over the years.
answers.Political background: My political journey has been characterized by a strong commitment to civic engagement and a deep belief in the power of democracy. I’ve actively participated in multiple campaigns and initiatives, striving to make a positive impact on my community and state. In 2019, I ran as a Democratic candidate for council-at-large in Old Bridge Township. In 2021 and 2023, I stepped up as a Democratic candidate for the New Jersey State Assembly in LD-12, driven by a desire to address critical issues facing our state.
answers.Why are you running for office?: I am running for office because my life experiences and values have instilled in me a deep sense of duty to serve my community and my state. One defining aspect of my background is that I am not a mother by birth, but I took on the role of raising my six younger siblings when our mother passed away 20 years ago. This experience taught me the importance of strong support systems, access to quality education, and affordable health care for all families, which are issues I’m deeply passionate about.
answers.Key election issue: In this election, my top priority is addressing the issue of housing affordability. Housing is a fundamental human need and a critical component of a stable and thriving community. Unfortunately, in New Jersey many residents, especially in my district, are facing significant challenges when it comes to finding affordable and safe housing options.
answers.Example of a successful project: One of the most rewarding volunteer projects I’ve been involved in was my work with a local nonprofit organization that focuses on youth mentorship and education. I led a project that aimed to provide educational support and mentorship to underserved youth in our community.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: One of the most challenging experiences I’ve faced in my life was when I had to step into the role of caregiver and guardian for my six younger siblings after the sudden passing of our mother over 20 years ago. At the time, I was still quite young myself, and taking on this responsibility was overwhelming, to say the least.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: I am committed to promoting common-sense gun safety measures here in New Jersey. While I respect the Second Amendment rights of responsible gun owners, I believe there’s a need for comprehensive gun safety reforms to protect our communities.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: Yes, I wholeheartedly support Governor Murphy’s initiatives to combat climate change in New Jersey. These initiatives are essential for reducing greenhouse gas emissions, transitioning to clean energy sources and protecting our environment for future generations.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: Addressing the cost of rent, housing affordability and property taxes in New Jersey is a multifaceted challenge that requires a comprehensive approach. As a legislator, I would prioritize several key strategies to tackle these issues.

answers.Plain: Age : 71 Hometown : Hazlet Occupation : Relationship manager and training facilitator for Wavelength Communications Skills Training Personal background : I am a third generation LD13 resident with blue-collar roots. My Rutgers bachelor’s degree in public policy has helped me in my pursuit for social justice, leading me to become involved in multiple activities. I was a Planned Parenthood trained escort, worked as a counselor for inner city kids in Plainfield, coached a young woman in the Boys & Girls Club of America to compete in a Youth of the Year scholarship program. I’ve worked as an account executive, helping companies create marketing campaigns, train their people to be better communicators and to better manage their internal operations. Essentially, helping people has been my main incentive over the years. Political background : Since high school, I’ve been politically active, canvassing for my chosen candidates as well as phone banking, creating marketing materials and running (twice) for Hazlet Township Committee. Why are you running for office : Monmouth County deserves better than our current state senator. It’s important to both be available for your constituents and responsive. I’ve heard too many complaints from voters about his lack of accountability and accessibility, which has made them reach out to senators in other legislative districts instead. I will hold town hall meetings and respond to calls. I am also a strong supporter of a woman’s right to choose. My opponent has consistently shown his disdain for women’s rights, most recently voting against the 2022 Freedom of Reproductive Choice Act. The GOP has stated its desire to follow up on the Dobbs decision by attempting to institute a nationwide ban on abortion. But if they can’t, they plan to outlaw the right for a woman to control her own body, state by state. We cannot afford for that to happen. We cannot be another Texas. I will fight to keep those protections. I also believe that gun safety has been sorely dismissed by my opponent. He has voted against virtually every gun-safety measure, including common-sense training requirements for anyone seeking to purchase firearms. Even law enforcement supports this obvious need. LD 13 voters can rest assured I will do everything possible to protect them from gun violence, without taking away their rights. As a Monmouth County resident, I’m appalled that we are virtually the only county that reassesses properties every year while the rest of the state does so every 5 years. My opponent pushed through a bill that mandates this, the Assessment Development Program. That is patently unfair and will change if I’m elected. Finally, I will not solicit or do business with the towns I represent, as my opponent does. I believe it’s an ethical breach and a conflict of interest. I hope to introduce legislation to codify this change. Key election issue : I am most adamant about women’s reproductive rights. We cannot afford to make women second-class citizens, which can very well happen if the Legislature turns Republican. Women are citizens. We shouldn’t be treated as second-class citizens. A bill to overturn the Assessment Development Program. A bill to disallow elected officials from doing business with the municipalities they represent. Support of all common-sense gun safety measures. An open-door policy for constituents to reach me. Regularly scheduled town hall meetings. Continued support and safeguards to protect women’s rights. Example of a successful project : When my nephew’s wife was deployed to Iraq, her squad was told there wasn’t enough body armor for them. I immediately contacted everyone from Gen. Janis Karpinski in Iraq to the National Guard commander in Pennsylvania under whose command my nephew’s wife reported, to the Pentagon. After multiple phone conversations and several days, these troops had their protective equipment. A client of mine wanted to train their entire company of almost 100 employees in meeting management and interpersonal skills over a two-day period. Their requirement was for this training to be ready to roll out within weeks. I put together a team of six facilitators, determined the correct training materials for each subgroup of employees, and facilitated training, while overseeing the other facilitators. The client’s outcomes met and exceeded their expectations. Example of a challenge faced : I have practiced martial arts for many years, but have only studied taekwondo since 2015. As virtually the oldest person practicing in my school, I have nonetheless managed to proceed from white belt (beginner) status to second-degree black belt since then. To reach that level, I had to learn and be able to perform 16 intricate “forms” or patterns, demonstrate multiple hand techniques and kicks, and use several of those methods to break three-quarter-inch boards. I was tested on these elements for every belt “promotion,” over the course of 90 minutes or more each time. I was determined to succeed – I never give up – so I spent not only class time learning and practicing, but also practiced on my own, over and over again, to perfect my moves. That’s not to say I’m perfect. The challenge is to always improve, always learn more, always help others in their quest. I continue to train and learn, and I welcome the ever-present challenges I face to constantly improve. On NJ’s gun laws : First and foremost, I’d work to improve the training requirements for gun ownership. Too many people don’t realize how compromised their safety and the safety of their children is. On the Murphy administration’s climate change proposals : Yes On housing affordability and property taxes : Affordable housing is a major issue that the GOP ignores, acting as though having lower income people in their neighborhoods will somehow destroy their quality of life. I would gather experts, from developers to housing advocates, to look into possible solutions. Campaign website

Age : 64 Hometown : Middletown Occupation : Full time legislator and adjunct professor Personal background : I was born in Brooklyn and moved with my wife and child to Middletown, New Jersey, in August 1994. I have a B.A., M.A. and Ph.D. in anthropology. I had a very successful career as a professional archaeologist, which led to teaching archaeology at Monmouth University as an adjunct professor. I spent eight years in the Christie administration as the director of the Office for Planning Advocacy and for a period, executive director of the Business Action Center. Political background : New Jersey State Assemblyman LD-13, 2020-present Monmouth County Freeholder, 2018-2020 New Jersey Department of State, Executive Director, Business Action Center, 2017-2018 New Jersey Department of State, Director, Office for Planning Advocacy, 2010-2018 Secretary, State Planning Commission, 2010-2018 Middletown Township Committeeman, 2005-2018 Mayor, Middletown Township, 2007-2008, 2010, 2013, 2016, 2017 Deputy Mayor, Middletown Township, 2006, 2009 Member, Legislative Committee, League of Municipalities, 2008-2010 Member, Middletown Zoning Board of Adjustment, 2003-2004 Member, Middletown Disaster Relief Fund Board of Directors, 2012-2015 Why are you running for office : I believe our country and way of life are being threatened like never before. I feel we need elected officials who are both fearless and correct on the issues. I want my three grandchildren (three under 3 years old) to grow up in the magnificent country that I grew up in, not a lawless, quasi-socialist welfare state. I am especially concerned about New Jersey and its future. The outflow of people moving to other states because of unaffordability, over-regulation, legislation that stifles personal freedom and constant government overreach into everyday life is something I want to change. Key election issue : Main – taxes, secondary – crime, parental rights, education, business climate, protecting the Jersey shore, etc. New Jersey has the unenviable distinction of having the highest property taxes, and worst business climate in the nation. Affordability must be addressed to stem the outflow of residents seeking less costly places to live. Introduced a bill to return the ETR to municipalities, which would dramatically lower property taxes. Voted against excessively increased spending by the governor. Co-sponsored and voted for legislation to help small business, increase property tax rebates and voted against increasing income tax rates for New Jersey residents. Example of a successful project : Successfully secured additional funding for mental health services and teen suicide prevention programs. Example of a challenge faced : Being in the minority party trying to move legislation through the process. I have overcome it by having a good relationship with colleagues on both sides of the aisle and bringing solid, constructive legislation to the Assembly. On NJ’s gun laws : I would stop attacking the honest, law-abiding citizen and concentrate on criminals who use illegal guns. That’s where the problem lies. Enforce the laws that are on the books and stop releasing dangerous criminals from jail. Overhauling bail reform would keep dangerous recidivist criminals off the streets. On the Murphy administration’s climate change proposals : I support all sources of energy and efforts to expand alternative energy. I do not support overreaching, costly mandates. On housing affordability and property taxes : Introduced legislation to restore the energy tax receipts (ETR) to municipalities, which would be a game changer for cutting property taxes across the state. Reinstitute regional contribution agreements (RCAs) to renovate existing housing where infrastructure already exists. Look to eliminate mandates that drive up local taxes. Work with Habitat for Humanity and similar organizations to expand and rehab affordable housing stock. Campaign website

Age : 69 Hometown : West Long Branch Occupation : Musician Personal background : Paul Eschelbach is a native of Red Bank. He holds a B.A. and M.A. from Rowan University, as well as an M.S.Ed. from Monmouth University. Paul spent nine years on the Red Bank Borough Board of Education. He taught in the New Jersey public schools for 41 years, 31 of those years were spent in the Long Branch Public Schools. He also taught in Atlantic Highlands and Little Silver. Mr. Eschelbach is a professional tuba and bass trombone player. He plays with three New York City orchestras: the United Nations Symphony, the Litha Symphony and the Orchestra Amadeus. He manages the Navesink Brass quintet. He also plays tuba in four community bands. He is a member of Local 309 of the American Federation of Musicians. Political background : Paul Eschelbach was a member of the Red Bank Borough Board of Education for three terms. He testified in front of the New Jersey Judiciary Committee in favor of same-sex marriage. He was president of the Long Branch School Employees Association for two terms. As a New Jersey Education Association member, Mr. Eschelbach was very active in politics. Why are you running for office : I believe there needs to be a change in Legislative District 13 leadership. The Assessment Demonstration Program, which was sponsored by Declan O’Scanlan, is unfair to Monmouth County residents. It needs to be replaced as it is unfair to taxpayers. It is important to preserve reproductive and LGBTQ+ rights in New Jersey. Key election issue : Property taxes To overturn the Assessment Demonstration Program and lower property taxes for seniors. Example of a successful project : Mr. Eschelbach advocated for LGBTQ+ marriage rights by testifying in front of the Assembly Judiciary Committee. Example of a challenge faced : Surviving on Social Security and a New Jersey pension. Reinstating cost-of-living asjustments to the Teachers’ Pension and Annuity Fund is important. Political advocacy through the NJEA Governmental Relations Department has been rewarding. On NJ’s gun laws : I believe anyone who gets a gun permit should go through mandatory gun safety classes. On the Murphy administration’s climate change proposals : I support Gov. Murphy’s climate change initiatives. Offshore wind and solar power need to be expanded. Free electric car chargers in convenient locations are important. On housing affordability and property taxes : Remove the ADP law that is in place in Monmouth County. Tax breaks for seniors need to be expanded. Campaign website

Age : 51 Hometown : Holmdel Occupation : Lawyer Personal background : I grew up in Moonachie, New Jersey. I thoroughly enjoyed growing up in North Jersey because the location provided me so many opportunities to watch sports and attend concerts. I spent my summers at the Shore, so when my husband and I were looking to buy our second home together as our family grew, we knew Monmouth County was where we wanted to live. I am a graduate of Rutgers (B.A. ’96) and Seton Hall Law School (J.D. ’99). After law school, I was the first clerk for the Honorable Jaynee LaVecchia, an associate justice for the Supreme Court of New Jersey. Thereafter, I worked in private practice for some of the state’s largest law firms. When I was elected to the Assembly, I started my own law practice to allow me the flexibility to balance my role as an assemblywoman with my law practice. Political background : Prior to being elected to the Assembly, I was a member of the Holmdel Board of Education, serving two terms, the last four years as president. When I lived in Nutley, I served as a member of the Nutley Board of Education for four years, serving my last years as vice president. I had to resign upon my move to Holmdel. Why are you running for office : I am running to continue to be a voice in Trenton for the great people of Monmouth County on the issues that matter to our constituents. We need to have a strong voice in Trenton to ensure our laws protect the public and permit law enforcement to perform their jobs safely and with protection from litigation. We also need to make sure that our schools are adequately funded so they may continue to address the academic damage caused by lockdowns during the pandemic. Schools are challenged because of teacher shortages and state aid cuts – we must fight to make sure we are supporting teachers, students and parental rights. We also need more people in Trenton to provide a common-sense perspective to the damaging energy policies being proposed – by causing people to have to choose only one form of car and taking away access to appliances dependent upon natural gas, Trenton Democrats have made New Jersey terribly unaffordable. We need to have Trenton focused on things that matter and place New Jersey on a trajectory of success. Key election issue : In order to encourage greater voter turnout, we need to do better as leaders to articulate to constituents the real impact of the policies being adopted in Trenton. For instance, here in Monmouth County, we have lost tens of millions of dollars in state aid for our schools. These losses are a direct consequence of failed state policies adopted by Trenton Democrats. As a leader in Monmouth County, it is incumbent upon me and my colleagues to explain to residents how these policies damage our students or teachers in our schools. We must also articulate the real effects of the energy policies that are said to be “green,” but make our state reliant on less-reliable energy sources that will result in skyrocketing energy costs. First, state aid cuts should be refunded to schools immediately, in those amounts lost during the pandemic. I’ll introduce legislation that would provide for those funding cuts to be reversed and instruct the Legislature to develop a fair state aid formula. We also need to continue to work on public safety risks caused by the catch-and-release policies that have resulted in the astronomical increase of car thefts and home invasions. While some of my legislation has been passed, there is more to do. I would advocate for the implementation of policies that protect students, encourage more students to seek a career in education, laws that would remove unnecessary barriers to pursuing a career in education. I would also advocate for policies to ensure parental rights and encourage even greater involvement for partners in children’s education. Finally, I would reverse those policies that have resulted in the devastating energy policies that will make New Jersey less affordable. Example of a successful project : New Jersey has encountered a significant uptick of car thefts in recent years. While the loss of a car is devastating alone, the tremendous hike in car thefts will likely lead to a tremendous hike in insurance rates in upcoming years. This is why we have to get this issue under control. When I was first elected, I was educated by members in law enforcement about the car theft issue. I therefore immediately drafted a bill package to address this issue. I am proud to say that some of the bills I introduced have been adopted during my first term, but I am hopeful that Monmouth County voters will give me a second term to continue that work so I could continue to address this issue for New Jersey residents. Example of a challenge faced : As a woman, it is always a challenge to be successful in fields that are mostly dominated by men. In order to be successful, I work very hard to be taken seriously by decision makers, and have had great success by working hard and by working well with others. On NJ’s gun laws : I would be more careful in developing laws in response to recent cases that have advised states to be more respectful of the second amendment rights afforded to law-abiding gun owners. Look, the violence caused by guns is overwhelmingly related to illegal guns and/or people who are not law-abiding citizens. New Jersey was not respectful of the constitutional rights afforded to citizens by the Second Amendment in drafting the legislation in response to the recent Supreme Court caselaw. I advocated to my colleagues in the Assembly to provide me the opportunity to help them draft a constitutional bill. My requests were ignored. But I remain confident that in upcoming years, my colleagues in the Legislature will work more closely with me to develop laws that will pass constitutional muster when challenged. On the Murphy administration’s climate change proposals : I do not. I would instead advocate for the adoption of an energy plan that is dependent on more diverse forms of energy, and not based upon an unattainable goal of being 100% green. The energy policy of the Murphy administration will cause great financial harm to New Jersey residents. While I am a supporter of green energy, it must be sustainable and affordable to ratepayers. On housing affordability and property taxes : We need to reverse those policies that make it terribly expensive to live in New Jersey. Campaign website

Age : 42 Hometown : Keport Occupation : Attorney and hospice nurse Personal background : I was raised in the Bayshore and have been living in Keyport for nearly nine years. I purchased my first home in Keyport at the end of last year. I work as a trial attorney for Levinson Axelrod serving the sick and injured by day. At night I work as a hospice nurse at Center for Hope Hospice. I feel strongly about giving back to my community. I am an active volunteer for the Monmouth County Medical Reserve Corps, participating in clinics and training. In October 2021, I received a Letter of Commendation from Task Force Liberty for my work in Operation Allies Welcome, in which I assisted in providing medical care to Afghan refugees at the joint base at McGuire-Fort Dix-Lakehurst. I also received recognition from the Monmouth County Commissioners earlier this year for my participation in the homebound vaccine project. Prior to working in law, I served professionally as an EMT, including in Newark and New Orleans. During that portion of my professional life, I responded to Hurricane Katrina as well as Superstorm Sandy. I maintained my career as an EMT while attending college, law school and nursing school. I also volunteered as both an EMT and a firefighter in Monmouth County from the time I was 16 through my early 20s. I am passionate about ensuring those afflicted by substance abuse and their families have the resources they need to recover. I currently serve as a trustee of the Wellspring Center for Prevention, a community-based non-profit dedicated to improving the health and well being of individuals, families and communities through substance abuse prevention and education. Although I am new to Wellspring I have volunteered in the recovery community for many years, providing direct mentorship for those affected by this disease. I am myself a person in long-term recovery from substance abuse. In April 2024 I will have 10 years of continuous abstinence. Everyone deserves the same resources that have allowed me to thrive and I am committed to working toward this aim. I am also disabled and have physical limitations, having recovered from a 14-level spinal fusion last year after suffering from a painful spinal deformity since childhood. With respect to my educational background, I graduated from Tulane in 2009 with a degree in media arts. I then attended law school at Rutgers-Newark and earned my J.D. in 2012. Following this, I received a certificate in practical nursing from Union County College in 2014 and became an LPN in 2015. I completed my associates in nursing in 2021 from Excelsior College and became an RN that year. I am also a certified CPR instructor. Political background : I have run for office once before. Last year I lost my race for Keyport Council. Why are you running for office : I am concerned about the politics of hatred and divisiveness that have become rampant in our country. I want to utilize my education, experience and energy to provide thoughtful leadership for all as well as to protect the rights of citizens from being infringed upon by extremist legislators. Key election issue : Reproductive freedom My opponents have called reproductive freedom “dangerous,” “radical” and “a hard no.” In a post-Dobbs America, I believe that legislators that hold these views are unfit for state office and the public must be protected from them at all costs. Such legislators need to be replaced regardless of party. Example of a successful projecy : I have tried several cases to verdict and achieved justice for my clients. Example of a challenge faced : I find that getting as much education as possible as well as really listening to shared experience from others who have been there is the solution to most problems I have encountered. On NJ’s gun laws : I support Gov. Murphy’s initiative to punish traffickers for crimes committed with guns. I also want to see more resources spent on getting ghost guns off the street to protect our police officers and citizens. I believe crimes committed with ghost guns should be harsher. On the Murphy administration’s climate change proposals : Yes. I believe in continuing to incentivize consumers who opt for climate-friendly transportation, appliances and energy in their homes. On housing affordability and property taxes : I believe that regionalizing schools would lower property taxes for many residents. I also believe that the annual reassessment program in my county has led to a greater tax burden for many residents and should be repealed. With respect to rent, I believe that the percentage of annual increase should be capped. Campaign website
