answers.Personal background: Piscataway, New Jersey; B.A. history/chemistry, University of Scranton; M.S. chemistry, M.S. environmental science, Rutgers University; L.L.D. law degree, Seton Hall University; teacher, Middlesex County College 1970-1981; lawyer 1981-present.
answers.Political background: Member Piscataway Environment Committee, member Piscataway Planning Board, member Piscataway Township Council, mayor of Piscataway, assemblyman 17th District, senator 17th District.
answers.Why are you running for office?: To protect New Jersey’s environment and mitigate the impacts of global climate change.
answers.Key election issue: Global climate change and what New Jersey needs to do to mitigate it. For next term – s2978 Accelerate NJ’s Renewable Portfolio Standard, s3992 NJ Grid Modernization, scr17 Amending NJ constitution to phase out fossil fuel plants.
answers.Example of a successful project: Elimination of single-use plastic bags from New Jersey supermarkets.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: Stable source of funding for the acquisition of preserved farmland, open space and historic preservation. After eight years of potential legislation, finally passed a constitutional amendment to dedicate 6% of the corporate business tax to the effort – about $150 million per year.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: Vote for even stricter gun control legislation.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: Yes. Take advantage of the federal IRA leveraging $300 million of societal benefit charges to make $500 million in New Jersey grid improvements. (Our grid is inadequate.)
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: Incentivize affordable housing. The new Stay NJ property tax relief program.

answers.Personal background: I am a Rutgers graduate, an Army reservist, who has lived across the street from the house I was born in. I have deep roots in my community of Somerset.
answers.Political background: I served on our local Planning Board, then served as Democratic chairman prior to my appointment to the General Assembly in October 2014 to replace an outgoing assemblyman.
answers.Why are you running for office?: To continue working toward making our state more affordable for all citizens, including in housing, job placement, education, health care and overall quality of life.
answers.Key election issue: Cost of living and affordability are for me the top issues in this election.
answers.Example of a successful project: Securing medical cannabis legislation that I helped co-author, which is now a national standard. In addition to laying the groundwork for medical cannabis, I was also instrumental in drafting the legislation that legalized adult-use cannabis.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: Seeking to revise and rewrite the 76-ye r-old antiquated liquor license laws in our state by building coalitions with stakeholders. I have crafted my bill A-5461, which I feel brings our residents closer to seeing common-sense changes in liquor licensing.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: I was the author of that bill, and we will wait for the courts to make a determination before moving forward.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: I strongly support maintaining the environmental integrity of our planet, however I take issue with certain aspects of the governor’s proposal. However, I look forward to continuing my discussions with the administration in those areas.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: I believe we have already begun addressing these issues with ANCHOR and Stay NJ, and will continue to work with my colleagues to seek additional remedies.

answers.Personal background: I am one of seven proud children born of Irish immigrants. I have lived my entire life in South Plainfield. I am a graduate of South Plainfield High School with a bachelor’s degree and law degree from Seton Hall University. I have been married to my wonderful wife, Anita, for 47 years and am the proud father of Heather and Tara and grandfather of Vanessa, Alexa, Brooke and Andrew.
answers.Political background: I was first elected to the General Assembly in 2001, taking office in 2002. I served until 2016, when I filled the Senate seat of Peter J. Barnes III when he was sworn in as a Superior Court judge.
answers.Why are you running for office?: To continue to work for my district towns but more important to encourage civility and bipartisanship in Trenton.
answers.Key election issue: Quality education and opportunity for all families to succeed.
answers.Example of a successful project: I worked closely with the New Jersey State Interscholastic Athletic Association and Athletic Trainers Society of New Jersey to implement safety guidelines designed to protect student-athletes from sudden cardiac arrest, traumatic brain injuries and exertional heat stroke. My legislation regarding concussion, heat participation and sudden cardiac arrest policies helped make New Jersey the national leader in managing catastrophic injury risks to high school athletes.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: Working together with legislators across the aisle and representatives from Johnson & Johnson, my legislation banning the manufacture, sale or promotion of personal care products containing microbeads became law. The bill was signed at Johnson & Johnson’s headquarters and was the template for federal legislation President Barack Obama signed into law.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: I support the gun laws passed by the Legislature.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: I support the governor’s initiatives. We must listen to everyone’s concerns and support necessary legislation going forward.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: There is no simple answer to this challenge. The ANCHOR program and StayNJ are good starts.
answers.Final thoughts: Restoring trust in government must be a top priority.

answers.Personal background: Assemblyman Robert J. Karabinchak is currently in his fourth term as representative of the 18th Legislative District. The 18th Legislative District consists of the Middlesex municipalities of East Brunswick, Edison, Highland Park, Metuchen, Milltown, South Plainfield and South River. Assemblyman Karabinchak currently serves as chair of the Assembly Special Committee on Infrastructure and Natural Resources and is a member of the Assembly Commerce and Economic Development and Assembly Telecommunications and Utilities Committee. He earned an associate’s degree in civil engineering and business management from Middlesex County College. A lifelong resident of Edison, he is a local business owner, working as president of Triform Construction in Metuchen. Assemblyman Karabinchak is married to his wife of 42 years, Linda. They are the parents of three adult children, Steven, Brian and Lori.
answers.Political background: Prior to representing the 18th Legislative District, he served the residents of Edison for eight years on the town council and has served multiple terms as council president and on its Finance Committee. Prior to that, he served eight years on the town’s Zoning Board of Adjustment and other municipal posts. He is also a Middlesex County Utilities Authority commissioner.
answers.Why are you running for office?: To serve the residents of District 18 in Trenton to ensure that their concerns and issues are represented at a state level.
answers.Key election issue: The main issues I am focused on in this election are protecting the environment and addressing climate change, improving infrastructure, and pedestrian and traffic safety.
answers.Example of a successful project: My proudest accomplishment of this year is the passage of A573, which would provide for the expedition of construction inspections. This bill will help with the housing shortage we are currently facing and allow for more affordable housing to be built quicker.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: Recently we passed a bill in the Assembly that would allow for more reclaimed asphalt to be used in the construction of roads (A4797). Though it was signed by the governor, there was a lot of back and forth between a lot of stakeholders. Everyone, including myself, gave up points that we wanted included in the bill. But overall, it was a great exercise on how the government truly works.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: Currently, I have a bill in the Legislature (A4657) that would require that all persons moving to New Jersey either permanently or temporarily be provided with explicit information regarding our gun laws. I support stronger gun safety measures and support the governor’s push for stricter gun laws in New Jersey.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: I overall support the Murphy administration’s initiatives to combat climate change and applaud his efforts to make New Jersey a leader in clean energy. I also believe that it is important we take a holistic approach to making the switch to clean energy and understand the impact on the economy and on families these initiatives may have on the future of all New Jerseyans.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: I would support measures to drive down the cost of rent and housing in New Jersey. During my time in the Legislature, we have been able to make strides in ending the outmigration of senior citizens by passing the StayNJ property tax rebate, and we will continue to make efforts to help families. Additionally, the last two state budgets have included an historic commitment to housing production, with $605 million going to housing production and programs like first-time home buyers’ down payment assistance.

answers.Personal background: I was born in India but grew up and went to high school in Brooklyn, New York. After I graduated from Xaverian High School in 1984, I relocated to East Brunswick, New Jersey. In addition to serving as an assemblyman for the 18th Legislative District, I am also an insurance broker, where I have gained valuable experience in the field as well as experience in the financial services field as a whole. Additionally, I am a proud father of three beautiful children, who always push me to be the best version of myself and protect their future.
answers.Political background: Before I became an assemblyman, I served on the East Brunswick Township Council from 2016 until 202,1 where I also served as council president. I also serve as a Middlesex County Democratic Committee member.
answers.Why are you running for office?: I am running for office because I firmly believe that the people of the 18th Legislative District, as well as the state of New Jersey, deserve a representative who tackles the issues that are necessary regardless how difficult they may be. Throughout my tenure as your assemblyman for the 18th District, I have had the opportunity to put forth legislation that has provided firefighters with health resources, protected survivors of domestic violence, prioritized mental health and so much more. If granted the privilege of continuing to serve the 18th District as their Assemblyman, I look forward to continuing to bring their concerns to Trenton so we can continue to build on what is undoubtedly the greatest state in the Union
answers.Key election issue: A key issue for me this election is continuing to build on the progress we have achieved in the 18th Legislative District. I want to make the key investments our families need to prepare for the future in New Jersey while keeping our communities safe. This means ensuring that our firefighters, police and EMS workers are supported both on the the job as well as when they are off duty, preparing our state for a sustainable future that takes into account the effects of climate change on our communities and our workforce and preparing our infrastructure at all levels in order to deal with the new realities it brings with it. And it means making sure that families can not only raise a family and work in our state, but also have the ability to afford to retire close to their families as well.
answers.Example of a successful project: In addition to StayNJ, another successful piece of legislation that I am incredibly proud to have led the charge on is recent legislation signed by the governor creating a pilot program for electric school busses, which represents the first real step toward a world where students do not have to have the smell of diesel be that which characterizes the start of their day.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: One challenge that I am seriously engaged in overcoming is the push to make sure that our local fire and EMS departments have the funding they need to continue to meet their needs when it comes to protecting our communities. When we consider cost-saving measures we must always remember never to pinch pennies from the back of public safety because our No. 1 responsibility as lawmakers is to keep all of those we are entrusted with representing safe. We have made serious progress in meeting this challenge, whether it be more frequent free cancer screenings for firefighters or our ongoing efforts to meet with stakeholders to figure out how we can address the most pressing needs of our public safety professionals.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: New Jersey has some of the most comprehensive gun safety laws in the entire country. Whether it be universal background checks, a ban on .50-caliber firearms, red flag laws or any of the other incredible gun safety policies we have passed into law, the data is clear that we are safer because of them.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: I am proud to stand by the governor as a partner in ensuring that New Jersey’s energy policy reflects not only the needs of consumers but also the needs of future generations that will come to inhabit a state we hope to be free of the deleterious effects caused by climate change and the continued utilization of combustion technologies where electrical solutions would be far more affordable and efficient. I look forward to continuing to work with our local, county and state partners to continue moving our great state forward toward a more sustainable future
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: This year I was proud to join Speaker Craig Coughlin and my colleagues in the Legislature in passing legislation that seriously addresses property tax burdens for all of New Jersey’s homeowners. As a proud supporter of these efforts, I believe we will see how policies such as StayNJ can make significant progress in ensuring those New Jerseyans that take pride in that identity can continue to live in the place where it was born. In addition to the incredible efforts undertaken by the speaker and my colleagues in the Legislature, I believe we must come to terms with the fact that the most reliable way to lower any tax burden is to more broadly spread out the cost of those services, which will only come about through the sharing of services and where appropriate, municipal consolidation. For context, California has 482 municipalities in which that state’s 40 million residents live. Our great state on the other hand has 564 municipalities in which our 9 million residents live. That is almost 100 more municipalities for 31 million fewer residents. If we wish to continue to address our affordability crisis, I believe this begins with continuing to seriously incentivize not only the sharing of services between municipalities but also the consolidation of municipalities where appropriate. This is all in addition to continuing to create sustainable programs that ensure each community meets their affordable housing obligations and continue to build on the overall progress we see each of our incredible towns making here in New Jersey.
answers.Final thoughts: I take such pride in being the first legislator of South Asian descent to represent my legislative district. I understand the responsibilities that come with that power. I promise to always lead with the best intentions, especially in servicing disadvantaged or marginalized communities. Additionally, I recognize the importance of diversity in all forms of government and want to continue to work hard on ensuring that every voice is heard.

answers.Personal background: Born in East Orange, New Jersey, to proud Irish parents and raised in the Vailsburg section of Newark, Sen. Joe Cryan represents New Jersey in all aspects of his life. He also serves as the executive director for the Middlesex County Utilities Authority, a position he’s held for five years. He and his wife, Kathy, live in Union Township with their dog, Scout.
answers.Political background: He was elected to the New Jersey General Assembly and represented Legislative District 20 (Elizabeth, Union, Roselle and Hillside) from 2002 until 2014. During this time, he served as an undersheriff for Union County. In the Assembly, he served as the majority leader and chaired or served on over a dozen committees, as well as holding the role of chair for the New Jersey Democratic State Committee from 2006 to 2010. He left the Assembly to pursue the office of Union County sheriff, to which he was elected in 2014. He was elected to the New Jersey State Senate in 2017, again representing the 20th District.
answers.Why are you running for office?: I’m running for office to fight for working families of the 20th District and to build upon the progress we’ve made since I have been in office.
answers.Key election issue: Protecting worker’s rights and standing with organized labor.
answers.Example of a successful project: I worked diligently to pass the Temp Workers Bill of Rights into law. It took a long fight and many powerful advocates to get this accomplished, but New Jersey will be forever changed for the better with this legislation.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: N/A
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: Ghost guns are a frightening trend in the United States, and as technology advances, it’s only going to get worse. I was happy to sponsor legislation that banned ghost guns in New Jersey, and I’m grateful to President Joe Biden for taking a step to implement this on a federal level.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: Climate change is a serious threat and New Jersey’s elected officials must do everything in our power to make our communities more resilient against them.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: I’ve worked with community partners, like Elizabeth’s Coalition to House the Homeless, to make sure our state’s budget helps people find a place to live. Housing justice has been a priority for me throughout my career and will continue to be.

answers.Personal background: Spent a lot of my life in the foster care system. Sometimes ending up on the streets with a drug problem. After a very bad experience, I had to decide whether to become a statistic or a part of society. I chose a part of society. Found a job that helped start to turn my life around. Worked for many years in small shops and big box stores, realizing they only cared about their bottom line. So, I decided to venture off on my own and start my own business. Over 25 years later I run a successful small business as well as a foundation for foster children and orphans, transitioning them into adulthood. Now it is my time to give back and truly help make a difference. Here is a video showing where I began and where I am. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e48_MIoBjCc Political background: I was a Board of Education member for the Township of Belleville and have been helping run campaigns for 20 years or more. I ran for City Council in my town and have run for commissioner in my county.
answers.Why are you running for office?: It does not matter to me if a person is Democrat or Republican. We all have almost the same goals in our hearts. For too long the government has taken advantage of us and is out of touch with some common-sense realities. Some are in it for power, some are in it for gain. We need to open our hearts and focus on what is in the best interest of the people. To me that will be the start to healing our country, state and local communities. I am tired of seeing politicians in it for their own gain and I want to make sure that the people have their voices truly heard. Here is a video of why I am running. https://carmenbucco.com/issues/why-i-am-running/ Key election issue: There are so many: taxes, education, safety and small businesses. Without these things working in harmony, you have no community.
answers.Example of a successful project: I started my business in a one-bedroom apartment with just 300 clients. I now have two stores and a road consultant.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: My childhood. I nearly died because of drugs and didn’t care about life because I had only me. Now I am a successful business owner.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: We need to really stop going back and forth with this issue. I feel both sides need to come together and use common-sense law. I don’t have an issue with the new law, but if you look at it, all someone has to do is carry extra magazines. We have so much technology. We need to use it to help stop the madness of mass shootings. Responsible gun owners should not have their rights infringed on.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: I do not support the initiatives. Not only is it costly, but it is also sea life as well. We again need to come together as leaders and find real solutions. These are Band-Aids to the solution and when they don’t work we have wasted taxpayer dollars. And homeowners would not be able to afford the infrastructure to make this successful. Look at the state that lost power because of no wind.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: We can rezone areas as retail residential that are not zoned for this use. Fix up abandoned properties. I agree with affordable housing because it could have made a difference in my life instead of living in boarding houses. We could use shared services to take a burden off the taxpayer. We should never sacrifice service and politicians need to stop creating jobs just to get votes.

answers.Personal background: I grew up in Fanwood and currently reside in Bernardsville. I received my bachelor of arts in English from the University of Mary Washington; my master of arts in English from Seton Hall University; and my doctor of philosophy in higher education leadership, management and policy from Seton Hall University. I spent many years teaching English at several high schools as well as two higher education institutions. After completing my Ph.D., I moved into higher education administration, where I primarily managed small-scale and large-scale initiatives associated with student conduct policies and management, Title IX education and student sexual violence prevention programming. After almost 20 years in education, I recently changed careers and now work in regulatory compliance for a telecommunications company. I have been a Bernardsville Council candidate and was named to the Bernardsville Council to serve from July 2021 to November 2021. Additionally, I have served on Bernardsville committees, including the Open Space Committee, the Cultural Arts Advisory Committee and as council liaison to the Department of Parks and Recreation. I currently serve as the president of the Rolling Hills at Bernardsville homeowners association and on the Main Street Bernardsville Promotions Committee. I also am a board member for Scotch Plains-Fanwood UNICO, Trilogy Repertory and Studio Playhouse. I have performed in community theater productions and as a background actor on many television shows and films. I have completed six marathons (including the New York marathon twice) and countless other races and enjoy riding my bike.
answers.Political background: I ran for Bernardsville council three times and was on the council in 2021, and I’ve been involved with the Bernardsville Democratic Committee since 2016. On a more general level, I have been involved in politics for many years, starting with when I interned for the Union County Office of Public Information during my summers in college. I’ve campaigned for campaigns, including Colleen Mahr’s first mayoral race in my hometown of Fanwood. For me, politics always has been about collaborating across the aisle to find ways to help residents in whatever ways we can.
answers.Why are you running for office?: The issues that matter to me – common-sense gun safety, cost of living versus wages, women’s reproductive rights, academic freedom, increasing mental health services, support for our unions, improvements to our infrastructure, and so forth – also matter to many other residents in my district and residents throughout the state. I want to work with other legislators to find solutions that will benefit everyone, not just people in one party or another. For me, it starts with having meaningful conversations and looking for common ground while also being sure to listen to the people who put their trust in us: our residents.
answers.Key election issue: Our transportation infrastructure – roads, bridges, and mass transit – has been in a precipitous decline for years. How many times have we boarded an NJ Transit train only to have it be delayed for one reason or another? The Gladstone Branch trains are over 40 years old and in dire need of replacement. How many roads and highways suffer from either too many potholes or uneven pavement – or both? Based on my conversations with residents, they’re very much aware of the decline, too. While we finally are seeing some progress (the eventual replacement of the Portal Bridge, the long-delayed construction of a new transit tunnel), we have so much more work to do if we want to stabilize our infrastructure.
answers.Example of a successful project: While working as assistant director of student conduct at New Jersey City University, I was project manager for an initiative to install a universitywide database that, when completed, would help us manage our student conduct cases. I worked with multiple university departments and stakeholders, as well as an external vendor, from start to finish, all virtually since we still were in the midst of COVID-19. We had regular meetings and were in constant communication about the progress of the database. This was a project close to my heart since I had written my dissertation on challenges of handling Title IX student sexual misconduct incidents in higher education. Not only did we improve the efficiency of managing our cases, but more important, we helped our students by making it much easier for them to report incidents anonymously and to get them the support services they needed.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: Writing my dissertation was one of the biggest challenges of my life. I’ve always found writing to come naturally to me, so I figured a dissertation would take awhile but wouldn’t be that difficult to write. I couldn’t have been any more wrong! I can’t tell you how many times I would complete a chapter draft and think I was in good shape, only to have my dissertation mentor tell me that the chapter needed a significant overhaul. Just when I thought I was done and ready to defend, she told me that I should postpone my defense for six months because my overall draft needed a great deal of work. Once I got over my disbelief, I doubled down and made the changes I needed to make. I went through each chapter and examined every sentence, every paragraph, every piece of data, and every reference. The end result: a dissertation (including references) of over 200 pages that was a much more powerful document compared to the first version. I had a successful defense, made a few post-defense revisions, and achieved my Ph.D.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: Common sense gun safety is absolutely vital to me. We are lucky to live in a state with such strict gun laws, and we need to ensure that those laws remain strict so that our residents are protected. I am firmly behind the federal appellate court’s decision to dismiss the lawsuit.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: I live in affordable housing and am very sensitive to the overall cost of living in New Jersey. For starters, we have to look at why wages have not kept up with the rise in cost of living and what we can do to find more balance. Part of that means ensuring the very wealthy residents are paying their fair share of taxes and not shifting the burdens to our lower- and middle-class taxpayers. That also would mean a careful review of our tax codes. I also would want to look for ways to stimulate wage growth across the board so that our businesses have more money to pay their employees, who – in turn – would have more money to put back into our state while being able to live more comfortably and not have to worry about basic provisions.

answers.Personal background: I am the mother of a college student and a career educator. I grew up in Pittsburgh as part of a large Irish-American family and have dual U.S. and Irish citizenship. I graduated from St. Mary’s College in Notre Dame, Indiana, with a degree in English and anthropology. After working for a couple of years in investment banking human resources, I became a teacher and have worked for the Rahway Public Schools since 2001. I currently live in Basking Ridge with my son, a dog and a couple of cats.
answers.Political background: I am a lifelong Democrat. I believe in Democratic values, such as protecting the environment, equality and justice.
answers.Why are you running for office?: I want to make New Jersey more accessible to all New Jerseyans, keep our children and schools safe, make childcare and eldercare more affordable, protect a woman’s right to choose and solve the infrastructure problems that plague our district.
answers.Key election issue: I believe we must fix eldercare. If we don’t turn our attention to the prohibitive costs and challenges of taking care of our aging parents, we are going to be at a crisis level within 10 years.
answers.Example of a successful project: In 2011, the Rahway High School Social Action Club, which I ran, was given an award by the U.S. Green Building Association for “Water Champions” – a water use and conservation study and awareness program run in collaboration with the Rutgers University Water Resources Program, the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection and AmeriCorps. We were also recognized with resolutions from the Rahway City Council and the Union County Board of Chosen Freeholders (now Commissioners) as well as by Kean University.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: Though I could never in a million years compare my experiences to frontline workers during the early days of the pandemic, I am a teacher and had a special set of challenges in the spring of 2020. Rahway was hit particularly hard – students lost family members, a close friend and colleague lost both parents to COVID within a month of each other, and we lost two colleagues and friends – one to a heart attack and another to suicide. So many of my students were anguished and depressed. Many simply disappeared – they never showed up for virtual instruction. Still others got jobs to help their families. It was difficult, but I found that committing myself to just being there professionally and emotionally for my students and learning more about how to teach in a remote situation actually helped me during that time. Students are resilient, but they still had significant needs. The school community adapted to become what they needed.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: New Jersey has the third-lowest rate of firearm deaths in the country thanks to our common-sense gun legislation. I support the recent federal appellate court decision to dismiss the lawsuit challenging the new state law that allows the state attorney general to bring public nuisance claims against gun sellers and manufacturers.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: In order to address the daunting cost of living in the Garden State, there are several measures the Legislature can take, including but not limited to bringing back the estate tax, reinstatement of the 7% sales tax (average residents only see a nominal benefit – it benefits the wealthiest 2%), closing the combined reporting loophole, reinstating the apportionment formula and doing away with opportunity zone tax breaks.

answers.Personal background: Born and raised in Newark, New Jersey. Graduated Morris County College with an A.S in Criminal Justice. Went to work as a police officer and detective for the Newark Police Department. Springfield resident for the last 16 years. Twice elected to township government and in the middle of my second elected term. I have been the public safety chair for the past five years.
answers.Political background: Elected to Springfield Township Committee in 2018 and re-elected in 2021. Have served as two-time committeeman, two-time deputy mayor and mayor.
answers.Why are you running for office?: To keep New Jersey residents and students safe and protect pro-choice rights.
answers.Key election issue: Public safety.
answers.Example of successful project: We have built and improved sports in Springfield with baseball and softball fields. All departments staffed and ready to help residents in my township
answers.Example of challenge faced: Guiding Springfield through two devastating storms back to back in 2020 and 2021. We worked day and night for six months to restore our town to pre-storm conditions
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: Gun laws in our state work well. I support gun ownership but also support background, mental and character checks for all. I also support full safety training, like I had to learn in the police academy.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: Yes, I support it but I would slow down the switch to electric. New Jersey isn’t ready to be fully electric within the next 10 years
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: Demand drives rent costs and that’s a hard one to take on. I do think there are ways to continue to improve the help hard-working families get as assistance but I would want to hear ideas from specialists in that area.
answers.Final thoughts: If keeping New Jersey safe is a priority for residents, they need to choose someone who knows and understands how it is done. I have the law enforcement experience needed to guide our district.

answers.Personal background: A.B. 1975 – Rutgers College. M.A. (urban and regional planning) and J.D. (law school) both 1979 – University of Iowa. Practice of law 1979-present (semi-retired). Planning consultant for historic preservation. I grew up first in Forest Hills, New York, then Fort Lee, New Jersey. (I went to high school in Englewood.)
answers.Political background: Republican since college. Active on Plainfield and Union County Republican committees since 1994, municipal chairman since 2014. Ran for local office twice, then General Assembly in 2015 and Senate in 2021. Served two terms on Plainfield Planning Board then five terms on Plainfield Historic Preservation Commission (chairman of the latter for nine years and currently vice chairman).
answers.Why are you running for office?: I now have time (due to retirement) to give even more to the community and the state than I already have, and giving my experience and skills makes me happy. I am a foe of political correctness and wokeness. I want to make New Jersey a prettier and happier place to live than what it has been turning into under the current aadministration. I want to save the quality of life that we have and improve it wherever possible.
answers.Key election issue: Property tax and school policies.
answers.Example of a successful project: I headed the complete replacement of Plainfield’s land use ordinance, and its first master plan in decades, when I was vice chairman of our Planning Board. I have headed our Historic Preservation system for many years, this being a town with 10 historic districts that put us on the map and largely define what we are.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: Being the only Republican in Plainfield’s city government, for a good 20 years, has posed challenges every day, in a town where many city officials have been unsympathetic to the historic districts. Dealing with them and making initiatives has been the best political experience one could ever hope for!!
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: I would leave our current gun laws alone. If we ever face an adverse decision in the courts, I would amend the laws with as little change as possible.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: The intention may be good but the governor’s initiatives could cause more harm than good, and should not be advanced where harm is foreseeable. He forgets that the electricity has to be generated someplace. I am very concerned about the offshore wind turbines, both because they are an imposition on the view, and because I am concerned (realizing the proof has not yet been received) about whales.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: As explained above, I would shift the cost of the schools away from local property tax. If a landlord’s taxes can drop by half, this saving can be passed along to tenants in the form of lower, or at least stable, rent. I am concerned about housing affordability, but this is a good first step.
answers.Final thoughts: This district, which is the southern half of Union County, has suffered far too long from the unresponsive and sometimes corrupt Democratic machine. This force is embodied thoroughly in my opponent, who has simply been in office too long. Let someone else have the Senate seat for a change, someone like me who is full of ideas.

answers.Personal background: I was raised in Clark and attended Arthur L. Johnson High School and the Taylor Business Institute. I have been married for 42 years and have seven children and nine grandchildren. I was employed in retail doing interior store display followed by two years with a financial institution in a few different positions. After having my children I went back to work in a local company as a clerk then spent 25 years in the employment industry doing executive search, specializing in the health and beauty aids discipline. I retired in 2007 because of health issues.
answers.Political background: While raising my children, I was invited by the mayor of Garwood – where we resided – to join the Public Celebrations Committee, serving as the vice chair then five years as the chairman. I served as the vice chair of the Republican Committee in the borough then as a member of the Borough Council. Upon completing the term, I trained to work on the Domestic Violence Crisis Intervention and was the Team Leader servicing five towns. I ran for the position of Union County Freeholder and was appointed associate vice chair of the Union County Republican Committee. I was elected as the Union County state committeewoman and in 2010 was elected to a four-year term as mayor of the Borough of Garwood.
answers.Why are you running for office?: I am running for office because I beleive I have some things I can contribute to making life in the Garden State better. I see some things going on in the education of our children that many residents do not agree with. I can contribute business knowledge, people skills, the ability to listen to the residents and do a good job as I did as mayor of our town. We have many problems here in our state and we need to be helped to get back on track
answers.Key election issue: Key in this election is our public education system. Our kids have among the lowest math proficiency skills in the nation. What happened? Our kids have fallen behind in reading and writing as well. I do not believe that COVID is the prime reason for this deplorable situation. They are not acquiring the skills that will allow these children to be productive members of society.
answers.Example of a successful project: Successfully formed and managed Union County’s first domestic violence team to assist victims at the time of crisis physically and acquainting them with available services and their legal rights. A very successful project was the planning and creation of the borough’s athletic complex to accommodate soccer, baseball and other activities. It was talked about for two prior administrations and went nowhere while wasting money on planning services. I was able to put the wheels in motion to successfully provide the community with a designated, modern facility which not only provided a place to compete but also generate income.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: As a Republican I won the mayoral election against a Democrat who had been a fixture as a council member and the mayor. I overcame the challenge by making a priority to campaign publicly, to use skills I acquired as a recruiter and managing a business.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: New Jersey has some of the toughest gun laws in the country but what we lack are adequate mental health treatment situations. We also do not pursue and punish those who commit crimes using firearms. Guns do not kill people, people do.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: I do not support the windmills because there are many unanswered questions pertaining to the effect they have on our environment and marine wildlife. My research has shown me that windmills actually cause the earth beneath to heat up more. Electric cars are expensive and there are inadequate charging stations. I believe Murphy is trying to do too much too fast. These things should be studied, researched and tested over a period of time.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: Union County has some of the highest tax rates in the country. Rents go up when taxes go up. I brought in the lowest tax increase in 18 years when I was mayor. Cutting spending is the way to go as I see it. Get rid of all extra frivolous spending. Housing is another issue altogether. It is one of supply and demand as well as what people are willing to pay for a home.
answers.Final thoughts: Candidate endorsement from New Jersey Public Health Innovation Political Committee, nominated for “Mayor of the Year” by the Gateway Chamber of Commerce for my support of small business.

answers.Personal background: I grew up in South Jersey-Buena, NJ – graduated from Vineland High School – attended Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania-School of Nursing on a full scholarship. I continued my education with a B.S. in health care administration and a master’s in health care administration. I worked initially as an intensive care unit nurse for eight years and then went into serving people with developmental disabilities in large state facilities in New Jersey; I consulted in this field in four other states and was CEO of three large state facilities serving people with developmental disabilities. I am currently a chief nursing officer at Matheny Medical and Educational Center, serving children and adults with developmental disabilities.
answers.Political background: I have been a lifetime Democrat, believing in Democratic values. I have previously run for Bedminster Township Committee, State Assembly and State Senate for LD23. This is a very Republican area, but I believe people are ready to consider alternatives.
answers.Why are you running for office?: I am running for office to help New Jersey stay on track with the Democratic values that have been enacted in our state thus far. I grew up with civil rights, gender rights and racial equality being enacted throughout the United States. Since 2016, these rights are being eroded and I want to continue to protect those rights at least for New Jersey. I am a mother and grandmother of seven grandchildren and I want them to have gender equality and a non-toxic environment in which to live.
answers.Key election issue: Property taxes.
answers.Example of a successful project: In my professional life, I led at least two facilities that were going to lose their licenses and assisted them back to recertification. That took meeting with all levels of staff and helping people feel empowered again to succeed.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: Going through a divorce was very difficult after 25 years of marriage; my ex-husband had depression, causing financial difficulties in both our finances and the business of my brother-in-law, for whom he worked. With strong family support, use of mental health services and spiritual services, I was able to work my way back to solid emotional and financial health.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: I would not change the current existing laws.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: My running mates and I all support the Murphy administration’s initiatives. Climate change needs to be addressed through a combination of measures, including solar, offshore wind, electric cars and greater use of electricity. We have also emphasized the need to retrofit existing buildings so that they are more energy efficient. This would significantly reduce the use of fossil fuels and create a considerable number of good-paying jobs for those already in the trades and for the additional people who would need to be hired to accomplish all that needs to be done. With both commercial/office buildings and a significant amount of the housing stock in this state pre-dating the most modern energy efficiency standards, this is a task that is long overdue, and which needs much greater attention.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: As stated earlier, I support the ANCHOR Program, which offers property tax relief to homeowners and renters, which would help make rent and housing more affordable through a reduction in property tax expenses. The addition of StayNJ relief would be a bonus for senior citizens, many of whom are on a fixed income and cannot afford to stay in their homes due to ever-increasing property taxes.

answers.Personal background: I was raised in Chatham, Morris County, and I currently have been living in Tewksbury, Hunterdon County, for four years. I have completed a bachelor’s degree in philosophy and a master’s degree in psychology during my educational journey. Working as an entrepreneur has taught me organizational management, negotiation and contract-writing skills, which I believe are all critical to public service and public utility offices as well, especially the Legislature. I strive to be a powerful listener, always answering to the needs of people on the ground before “special” interests.
answers.Political background: I have always been a Democrat. New Jersey is such a wonderful place to live, with such a high quality of life, because we have such a robust public sector and I believe we have the Democratic Party to thank for this. Furthermore, it is the Democratic Party in the form of Craig Coughlin’s StayNJ project that is doing the most to help offset the burdens of property taxes, which is a core and legitimate issue to New Jersey politics. Lastly, I was a supporter of the Tom Malinowski campaign locally during the past cycle and was a surrogate for Andrew Yang when he was running his presidential race with the Democrats.
answers.Why are you running for office?: I am running for office for many reasons but if I had to identify one, it is the need to increase civic engagement in this district. By considering diverse groups of constituents, going to all types of regular meetings and exploring common ground we can absolutely change the culture and deliver improvements in government that we all deserve, which ultimately is why I want to continue to do the work.
answers.Example of a successful project: I started a small video production business in South Korea when I lived there that turned into a boutique marketing and communications firm, serving huge clients, like Porsche, Marriott and Pfizer. However, we were also able to take smaller clients during that time as well, and we could hardly differentiate between the importance of a contract based upon the amount of money we thought it would bring. I did it all by pounding the pavement, relentlessly, and I intend to do the same amount of legwork when I am in office.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: The death of my mother was profoundly difficult for me. She had suffered with brain cancer for over a year before requiring hospice. I overcame the challenge of caring for her and my young family simultaneously by learning many types of mindfulness practices. I think applying those skills to any sort of high-pressure or stressful situation is key.

answers.Personal background: I grew up in El Paso, Texas, as the son and grandson of a local grocer. I have been wealthy and homeless, and I have worked in the trades and gone to college. I straddle rural and urban America, white- and blue-collar America. So does my district. LD23 deserves to be represented by someone who knows what it is like to worry about your next paycheck, or an injury keeping you from the hours you need, but who can also appreciate how much it can sting when you see just how little of a bonus actually goes into your pocket.
answers.Political background: I don’t have one. I am a normal guy who wants to make a difference.
answers.Why are you running for office?: New Jersey, our beautiful Garden State, has given me everything. I got a new start, a wonderful wife, an education from Rutgers and a career I love here – and it’s time to pay back my community and the state I love. I am running to represent the younger generations, to make sure we have a voice and to make sure there are climate knowledgeable folks in Trenton representing my district.
answers.Key election issue: Property taxes.
answers.Example of a successful project: I do it every day. I plan and complete projects on the farm and at work I am effectively a project manager with security analyst training and expertise.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: My life has been a challenge. I am adopted, my birth family is divorced, I was a childhood epileptic and I now have migraines, vertigo and cluster headaches under management. I have been homeless, with nowhere to turn. I have suffered poisoning and traumatic injury. I relocated from Texas to New Jersey when I had nowhere to turn – my health was poor, so I couldn’t earn a living, and I had no money, no family who could support me and no prospects. My wife gave me a new chance here in New Jersey and I embraced it. I have built a good life here through resilience, a good work ethic and being willing to accept a hand up when I needed one.

answers.Personal background: Lifelong resident of Wantage Township in Sussex County. Graduate of High Point Regional High School. My wife Jill and I have three adult children and one grandson.
answers.Political background: I have been an assemblyman since March 2013. I am the deputy Republican whip, and I currently serve on the Assembly Agriculture & Food Security Committee and the Assembly Labor Committee. I served on the Sussex County Freeholder Board from June 2010 until taking the oath of office as an assemblyman. I served on the Wantage Township Committee from 2004 to 2009 and was mayor three times. I served on the board of directors for Sussex Rural Electric Co-op. I have been an active member of the Wantage Fire Department since 1989 and was the department’s chief in 2001 and 2002. I was the elected Republican state committeeman for Sussex County from 2009 to 2021 and serve as a Sussex County Republican committeeman. I am also a life member of the National Rifle Association, the New Jersey Farm Bureau, the Sussex County Chamber of Commerce, the National Federation of Independent Business and Newton Moose Lodge.
answers.Why are you running for office?: New Jersey needs legislators who live in the real world. I own a family business, and I am the only farmer who serves in the Legislature. I know what it is like to not only get my hands dirty, but to meet a payroll, hire and fire, and make a living operating a seasonal business. Too often legislators and bureaucrats make decisions without realizing the practical effect they will have on the average person or the average business owner, and I use my real-world experience to try and make a difference for my constituents and be their voice.
answers.Key election issue: We must continue the fight back against all of the Murphy mandates and his Democrat enablers in the Legislature. Their unpopular policies are on the ballot this November, and the voters know it. Whether it’s his disregard for parental rights and the promoting of controversial sex ed standards and other controversial curriculum and gender issues in schools to banning gas stoves, natural gas and forcing everyone to buy electric vehicles to his massive school aid cuts to most school districts I represent, which has caused property tax hikes and educational “disopportunity,” Murphy and the Democrats’ policies are harming the average family.
answers.Example of a successful project: One of the most successful projects I undertook happened while I was fire chief. We advocated for enactment for the Length of Service Awards Program for Wantage Township. This program is essential for retaining our current volunteer first responders and recruiting new ones.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: I think many people will share the same negative feelings of the COVID19 pandemic. We had the challenge of keeping my family-run business afloat during the lockdown and slow reopenings. We had to reinvent our business to a drive-thru and while not being allowed to have our gift shop and restaurant open. Thanks to our wonderful visitors, we persevered and made it through this terrible time.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: New Jersey’s draconian gun laws need to be reformed to comply with the Second Amendment and the Bruen decision. I opposed all of Murphy’s and the Democrats’ gun laws that have been enacted since he took office in 2018. I would start with repealing all of these recent laws, including and especially A4769, which severely limited our rights to carry concealed and is knowingly written to run afoul of the US Supreme Court. We must recognize in New Jersey the fact that the right to keep and bear arms and the right of self-defense are God-given rights, natural rights that have predated the existence of governments.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: I absolutely oppose the Murphy administration’s energy master plan. I do not believe in eliminating natural gas as an energy source, and I am opposed to mandating the electrification of homes, businesses and automobiles. This will come at a huge cost to homeowners and energy consumers and has the potential to wreck the state’s economy. People need reliable energy sources. Natural gas is much cleaner than coal, and we should be promoting its usage as well as looking into the possibility of building another nuclear reactor for our energy needs.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: As an assemblyman, I have sponsored over 100 bills to address property taxes – legislation on tax reduction, government transparency, shared services and the elimination of wasteful spending in order to lower property taxes.
answers.Final thoughts: My running mates, Assembly candidates Dawn Fantasia and Mike Inganamort, and I have been endorsed by the National Rifle Association Political Victory Fund, the National Federation of Independent Business, NJ Right to Life State PAC, the NJ Outdoor Alliance, the NJ Second Amendment Society, NJ Public Health Innovation PAC and Team Protect Your Children NJ. I have also been endorsed by the NJ State Nurses Association and named a Parental Rights Champion and Recommended Candidate by the NJ Family Policy Center.

answers.Personal background: The CFO of a not-for-profit organization, with responsibility for financial reporting, facilities and risk management. I held various roles in top management, such as vice president finance/acting CFO for Planned Parenthood, and similar roles in other organizations. I hold a B.S. in business management and am a chartered professional accountant, a certified general accountant, a fellow of the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants, a certified forensic accountant, a registered forensic investigator, a member of the American Board of Forensic Accounting and a Leadership Morris graduate, class of 2018. In April 2022, I received the NJBIZ Leaders in Finance award.
answers.Political background: Before migrating, from a young age I was actively engaged in pushing for political reform in my country of birth, Guyana. My activism finally led to my involvement in brokering the “Herdmanston Accord,” also known as the “St. Lucia Statement,” a peacekeeping agreement Guyana’s two major political parties made in 1998, to end the political upheaval in the country.
answers.Why are you running for office?: I am running to effectively represent the constituents of my district and make a difference by working with members on both sides of the aisle on behalf of the people. I believe that our government should be accountable, responsible, transparent and inclusive. We have underfunded schools, poor and inadequate infrastructure that is unattractive to new business, very little rent protections for tenants, young people cannot afford to access post-secondary education without incurring high debt and there is no alternative for them, high taxes, environmental issues like deforestation of Sparta Mountain and the Tennessee pipeline expansion project, among others. I believe that elected officials should put people first over party, and I intend to do so once elected.
answers.Key election issue: Access to education for everyone, from high school to college.
answers.Example of a successful project: A skilled training program funded by CIDA and IADB via a voucher program in Guyana. The project was voted the most efficiently and effectively run funded program by the review team in 2002. I was the finance officer on the project.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: Overcoming inequity with respect to my career advancement as a person of color.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: First of all I respect the right to bear arms. I would revise the law prohibiting license holders to carry their concealed weapons in public places, in-person interview of character witnesses, and justification for firearms need, among others. I would strengthen the law by requiring a comprehensive mandatory training course for applicants, a minimum of eight hours, a combination of theory and practical examination in gun use, safety, storage, etc. Implement a 25-day waiting period for due diligence, background checks, etc. Then issue a five-year license with a five-day waiting period for renewal, pending background checks, as situations can change. I would ensure that the red-flag law is enforced after rigorous investigations to safeguard against personal bias and malicious complaints.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: I agree that climate change is an issue; however, conversion must be by phased transition and there should not be mandates imposed on citizens, with timelines for conversion. Conversion should be a consumer choice. There is also a cost factor; for example, electric cars are not affordable by any means, even with incentives, for moderate-income persons, much less for low-income individuals; no one can determine the real replacement cost for solar panels, among others. I also have a moral issue with respect to cobalt mining, a major component of batteries from a human rights perspective. We should not do away with fossil fuel, but we can enact more regulations to minimize pollution.
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: I would have a rent stabilization program with consultation with tenants and property owners. There is a need for more affordable housing development with more incentives, such as the Neighborhood Revitalization Tax Credit programs and funding from HUD, to make home ownership more affordable. We need to halt property tax increases in NJ. Some areas to address this would be to work with school districts on their budgets and consolidating classrooms for more efficiency; attract new businesses or bring them back to the state by ways of incentives, and shared services partnerships by nearby towns, among others.
answers.Final thoughts: As a moderate Democrat, I believe that elected officials should put people first over party, something I intend to do when in office. I would not vote for or introduce any bill until there is full consultation and agreement with my constituents. I am not afraid to speak truth to power and will be the voice of the people in Trenton. As an experienced professional, I believe that we need to restore accountability, responsibility, transparency and inclusivity to our government, and I will hold all to account.

answers.Personal background: I grew up in Sussex County, in Ogdensburg, and have resided in Franklin Borough for the past 12 years. I’ve worked in NJ education for the past 17 years in both traditional public schools and public charter schools as a teacher, vice principal, middle school principal and now a district administrator, and I vehemently support parents’ rights and school choice. A proud mom of three, I earned my undergraduate degree from Davis and Elkins College in West Virginia, and a master’s degree in educational leadership from Capella University as a recipient of the National Project Working Mom national scholarship program.
answers.Political background: For the past eight years, I have been honored to serve the community that has been so supportive of me and my family, and now having the support of retiring Sen. Steve Oroho and Assemblyman Hal Wirths, and a running mate in Assemblyman Parker Space is nothing short of humbling. As a former Franklin Borough councilwoman/council president, former member of the Franklin Borough Zoning Board and Economic Development Committee, and as a current Sussex County commissioner serving my second term, I am the county liaison to the Division of Health, Sussex County Chamber of Commerce, Economic Development Partnership, Department of Central and Shared Services, Capital Budget Committee, Sussex County Community College and the Sussex County Arts & Heritage Council. I have the experience necessary at both the municipal and county levels to express our needs in Trenton with fidelity.
answers.Why are you running for office?: First and foremost, I am running to protect our beautiful northwest corner of New Jersey. I was raised and went to school in Sussex County, and I have raised my children here; I believe the preservation of our values and way of life is critical. Under liberal one-party rule in Trenton, our state is on a path to both economic destruction and cultural ruin. Whether it’s rising taxes that drive out our residents and jobs, extreme school curriculum that indoctrinates our children, or constant attacks on our right to bear arms and the right to life, we need conservative voices in Trenton who can fight back – and who can win. I’ve been a fighter my whole life. As a single parent, I put myself through school, built a successful career, and won campaigns for both local and county office. As a public charter school educator, I am a staunch advocate for parental rights and school choice. I will be prepared on day one to be a voice for regular people just like me.
answers.Key election issue: As a lifetime NRA member and the victim of a gun crime, it’s time that we enact measures that do not stifle our constitutionally protected right to keep and bear arms. The Murphy administration inexplicably believes that by enacting more restrictions for law-abiding gun owners, illegal guns used to commit crimes will magically disappear. Instead, we must reduce the illegal use of firearms in the commission of crimes and in gang activity.
answers.Example of a successful project: One of my most fulfilling projects in public office was implemented in my final year serving at the local level in Franklin Borough. Local volunteer first responders approached the council regarding the possible implementation of a Length of Service Awards Program, a 401(k)-like pension program for members of volunteer fire companies and rescue squads that meet a locally set minimum number of calls or program activities. Operating under state law and rules and approved by voters, participating municipalities make annual payments per year, per volunteer, to individuals who meet the strict emergency volunteer requirements. The funds are placed into individual accounts for each member.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: In 2020, I was the deputy director of the Sussex County Freeholder Board, and during that time, 82 residents and two employees of the Andover Subacute and Rehabilitation Center died during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic; 17 bodies were found on site in a makeshift morgue. After expressing grave concerns directly to the NJDOH, with the county making over 120 documented contacts with the state regarding this critical emergency, Sussex County filed two Open Public Records Act requests in May of 2020 in an attempt to get answers as to what happened at this state-regulated facility. Sussex County was relentless in our pursuit for assistance and answers, quite literally hounding the NJDOH and demanding assistance from the NJ National Guard. To that end, the state has demonstrated the persistent inability to manage safe oversight of long-term care facilities (as again evidenced by the tragedies that continue inside veterans homes in Menlo Park and Paramus).
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: The Second Amendment is enshrined in the United States Constitution; regardless of law, New Jersey’s continuous “gun grab” persists, whether it be under Gov. Murphy’s unconstitutional roadblocks to legal gun ownership by charging increased, discriminatory fees in order to legally obtain firearms, or red-flag laws that now rely on “good cause” and not the legal standard of “probable cause” for search and seizure.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: I am opposed to Gov. Murphy’s energy master plan. I do not believe in eliminating
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: New Jersey has the highest property taxes in the nation as well as having some of the highest income and corporate taxes in the country. All of this puts us at a competitive disadvantage in attracting new businesses and jobs while keeping families and current employers here. If elected to the Assembly, I will sponsor legislation on tax reduction, government transparency and the elimination of wasteful spending in order to lower property taxes as well as state taxes.
answers.Final thoughts: To date, I am endorsed by the New Jersey Second Amendment Society and have earned an “A-Q” rating from the NRA – the highest rating a candidate can earn for an office they have yet to occupy. Additionally, I am endorsed by the New Jersey Outdoor Alliance, New Jersey Right to Life, NJPHIPAC, NFIB and NEW JOBS PAC. In Trenton, I will continue to represent the conservative values of northwest New Jersey and ensure our region has a voice that fights to defend our values.

answers.Personal background: I am a career accounting professional, a lifelong volunteer and a political activist. I am married with six children. I am the daughter of immigrant parents and the first in my family to seek political office. I have a bachelor’s degree in accounting and a master’s in business administration. I have more than 30 years of professional experience in both for-profit and nonprofit settings. I am a trustee for the Mount Olive Public Library, a member of the Environmental Commission, a former member of the Recreation Advisory Committee and a board member of my HOA.
answers.Political background: I got involved in politics after 2016, and I voted for the first time in 2020 after becoming a citizen. I am the former treasurer, current district leader and vice chair of the Mount Olive Democratic Committee. I ran twice for public office: in 2021 for Mount Olive Town Council and in 2022 for Morris County commissioner. I campaigned for Tom Malinowski in 2022 and attended many fundraisers to support local, state and federal candidates.
answers.Why are you running for office?: I look around at what is happening in our nation today with democracy hanging by a thread, our rights being taken away, our planet being exploited, etc., and I ask myself, is this the legacy we are leaving for our children and grandchildren? The answer is no. We’ve seen what happened with Roe v. Wade; 50 years later, we are still fighting for the same rights women fought for in 1973. I was 1 year old. We can’t let that happen; we need to stand up now and effect change to ensure the future generation doesn’t have to repeat the vicious cycle, so I am running to effect change in a positive way for all New Jerseyans.
answers.Key election issue: There are many issues I would like to see addressed, but if I had to choose one, it would be education, because I believe that education is the key. Nelson Mandela said it best: “Education is the most powerful weapon which you can use to change the world.” With an educated population, we ensure that people are equipped with the skills needed to become successful. When the population is educated and successful, the communities and the state benefit as well. I would like to see a program that automatically enrolls students from high school into community colleges and technical schools. I would propose more state funding for public education, including community colleges and technical schools. Not everyone would want to take the four-year traditional college route; for those who can’t, there should be options. We need skilled workers in NJ; we need more electricians, plumbers, mechanics, etc.
answers.Example of a successful project: I’ve worked for corporations for more than 30 years, and over that time I’ve done a lot to enhance the process and make things more effective. For instance, I’ve automated a lot of tedious and routine chores to free up my time so that I can concentrate on more crucial and complex jobs. I am constantly searching for methods to make procedures more efficient, since I believe in working “smarter, not harder.” As a trustee on the library board, I used my expertise in financial reporting to streamline the financial reporting process in the early going. Trust me when I say that everyone appreciated it.
answers.Example of a challenge faced: I was very shy growing up, never seeking the spotlight, always working in the background, so it was very challenging for me to run for public office. I had to really step outside my comfort zone, especially when I am at public events where I have to speak or when canvassing and talking to voters about my campaign, myself, etc. I hate talking about myself; I always believe that my actions should speak for me. I always say “action speaks louder than words.” But I learned that when running for public office, you have to speak, so I did some online training on public speaking. With practice comes confidence, and even though I was very nervous at first, eventually I was comfortable enough to speak. I am still nervous, but I do it anyway.
answers.On NJ’s gun laws: I would seek to maintain NJ’s tough gun rules because I think they make our state one of the safest in the nation. According to research by Giffords.org, it appears that NJ lacks rules governing the surrender of firearms, as well as laws governing assault weapons and “ghost” weapons. I would look into these issues and work to remedy these loopholes. I think there should be a balance between our Second Amendment rights and public safety.
answers.On the Murphy administration’s climate c: I support the Murphy administration’s initiatives to combat climate change. I believe that these initiatives are necessary to reduce New Jersey’s reliance on fossil fuels and to create a cleaner, healthier environment. Climate change is real, although some would like to think differently. According to the 2020 NJ Scientific Report on Climate Change, “As atmospheric levels of carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases increase, New Jersey will experience significant direct and secondary changes in its environment. These include increases in temperature, variability in precipitation, frequency and intensity of storms, sea-level rise, ocean acidification, and the associated impacts to ecological systems, natural resources, human health and the economy.” Human activities, particularly the emissions of heat-trapping greenhouse gases from the burning of fossil fuels and land use changes like deforestation, have increased atmospheric carbon dioxide concentrations by more than one third since the early 1900s (Bereiter et al. 2015) and are now the primary driver of climate change (Global Change2020).
answers.On housing affordability and property ta: There are many factors contributing to housing insecurities, such as the high cost of rent, lack of affordable housing, unemployment due to COVID-19, etc.
answers.Final thoughts: When elected I will work for the people, which means I will be out in the various communities engaging the residents to get feedback on issues that are important to them so I can propose and support legislation and policies that will benefit them.
